text: The centre and its strategical significance
zh: 中心及其战略意义

text: The knight on e5 and d5 (e4 and d4). The pawn centre. Attack with the central pawns. “Hanging” pawns.
zh: e5和d5（e4和d4）上的马。兵中心。以中心兵发动进攻。悬兵。

text: The part of the board which includes the squares e4, d4, e5 and d5 is called the centre. These squares are called central.
zh: 棋盘上由e4、d4、e5和d5四格构成的区域称为中心，这四格称为中心格。

text: The arrangement of the pieces in the centre, from where they operate in several directions, might serve as a basis for the construction of very active plans. Many different ideas and combinations have been carried out on this basis.
zh: 棋子位于中心，便能向多个方向发挥作用，为制定积极主动的计划奠定基础。许多不同的构想和战术组合正是由此产生的。

text: At the end of the last century the famous American chessplayer, Pillsbury, was able to win a number of interesting games where the basis of the initiative was the planting of a knight on e5. In the 20's and 30's of our century, a plan, where the whole object was the occupation of the d5 square (for Black - d4) with the knight, became increasingly pronounced. The centralised knight, supported by pawns, hampered the activity of the opponent, guaranteed a lasting initiative and frequently brought the champions of such ideas success.
zh: 十九世纪末，美国名将皮尔斯伯里以马占据e5作为夺取主动权的基础，赢下了多盘精彩对局。到了二十世纪二三十年代，以马占据d5格（黑方则为d4格）的计划越来越引人注目。受到兵保护的中心马可以限制对手的活动，确保持久的主动权，常常为采用这一构想的棋手带来胜利。

text: We return, in the first instance, to Pillsbury's idea, introduced into international practice at the 1895 Hastings tournament in games against Tarrasch and Schlechter. These proceeded identically up to the 11th move:
zh: 先来考察皮尔斯伯里的构想。他在1895年黑斯廷斯大赛对塔拉什和施莱希特的两局中，将这一构想引入国际赛场。两局在第11步之前的进程完全相同：

text: The so-called Orthodox variation of the Queen's Gambit. This variation is also met in our day and consequently continues to be developed, but the proportion of games with it, in comparison with the end of the 19th and the first two decades of the 20th century, was reduced owing to the opening systems which arose on the basis of the reply 1... Nf6. The fact should also be taken into account that methods of play have considerably improved for Black, and White does not succeed in easily obtaining a positional superiority as happened in Pillsbury's time.
zh: 这是后翼弃兵中所谓的正统变例。这个变例至今仍有人采用，也还在继续发展。不过，与十九世纪末及二十世纪头二十年相比，它在实战中所占的比例已经下降，因为以1... Nf6为基础的各种开局体系兴起了。还应指出，黑方的下法已有显著改进，白方不再像皮尔斯伯里时代那样容易取得局面优势。

text: This was nearly always played in the old days. In itself, the plan with the development of the bishop on b7 looks quite logical and does not arouse any objections on principle. But a principal - is a principal and concreteness - is concreteness. Pillsbury was the first to have doubts about the then generally accepted method of play for Black. In the course of time, more and more the shady side of the move... b6 followed by... Bb7 was revealed, and now there is a decided preference for 7... c6 with the aim of preparing an invasion of the Black knight on e4. (7... Ne4 at once is not possible, in view of 8. Bxe7 Qxe7 9. cxd5 Nxc3 10. Rxc3 exd5 11. Rxc7.) Besides this, 7... c6 allows him, in the event of 8. Bd3, to bring about a favourable relaxation of tension in the centre by 8... dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5. Practice has shown that in this way Black succeeds in overcoming the difficulties with the development of his queen's flank. **8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5**
zh:
过去几乎人人都这样走。把象出到b7的计划本身合乎逻辑，从一般原则上看也无可非议。但原则归原则，具体局面归具体局面。皮尔斯伯里是第一个对当时公认的黑方下法提出怀疑的人。随着时间推移，...b6接...Bb7的缺点逐渐显露，如今人们已明显偏向7... c6，准备以马侵入e4。（立即7... Ne4不行，因为8. Bxe7 Qxe7 9. cxd5 Nxc3 10. Rxc3 exd5 11. Rxc7。）此外，7... c6还使黑方能在8. Bd3之后走8... dxc4 9. Bxc4 Nd5，以有利方式化解中心的紧张。实践表明，这能帮助黑方克服后翼出子的困难。

**8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5**

text: As distinct from the game with Tarrasch, where Pillsbury lost a tempo - 11. Re1, allowing Black to take over the initiative after 11... c4 12. Bb1 a6 13. Ne5 b5 14. f4 Re8 15. Qf3 Nf8 16. Ne2? Ne4!, against Schlechter he continued **11. Bb1 Ne4 12. Bf4 Nxc3 13. Rxc3 c4 14. Ne5**
zh:
对塔拉什时，皮尔斯伯里以11. Re1损失一个先手，使黑方在11... c4 12. Bb1 a6 13. Ne5 b5 14. f4 Re8 15. Qf3 Nf8 16. Ne2? Ne4!之后夺得主动权。而对施莱希特时，他改走：

**11. Bb1 Ne4 12. Bf4 Nxc3 13. Rxc3 c4 14. Ne5**

text: This is Pillsbury's initial position for attack on the king's flank, based on the position of the knight e5.
zh: 这就是皮尔斯伯里以e5马为支点、准备进攻王翼的基本阵势。

text: Beginning from this time, Pillsbury's strategical idea was frequently employed both by himself and many other players.
zh: 从此以后，皮尔斯伯里本人和许多其他棋手都经常采用这一战略构想。

text: Here are a number of examples of the purposeful exploitation of the position of the knight on e5.
zh: 下面的几个例子，展示了如何围绕e5马的位置，有目的地展开行动。

text: Queen's Gambit
zh: 后翼弃兵

text: White: R.Charousek
zh: 白方：R. 恰鲁塞克

text: Black: S.Alapin
zh: 黑方：S. 阿拉平

text: (Berlin 1897)
Here, this continuation is even weaker than on the 7th move.
zh: 这一后续手段在这里比第7步时采用还要弱。

text: The absence of the knight on f6 was exploited very energetically in the game Pillsbury-Swidersky, played in the international tournament at Hannover 1902: 5. cxd5 exd5 6. e4! dxe4 7. Ne5! with the threat Bc4. After 7... Bd6 8. Qg4! Kf8 9. Bc4 Bxe5 10. dxe5 Qd4 11. Bd5! White obtained a direct attack on the king, stuck in the centre, and achieved victory already on the 30th move. **5... Nf6 6. cxd5 exd5 7. Bb5+**
zh:
1902年汉诺威国际大赛中，皮尔斯伯里对斯维德尔斯基有力地利用了黑马尚未出到f6这一点：5. cxd5 exd5 6. e4! dxe4 7. Ne5!，威胁Bc4。7... Bd6 8. Qg4! Kf8 9. Bc4 Bxe5 10. dxe5 Qd4 11. Bd5!之后，白方对滞留中心的黑王发起直接进攻，并在第30步获胜。

**5... Nf6 6. cxd5 exd5 7. Bb5+**

text: The planned placement of this bishop is the d3 square, but White gives the check in order to provoke the reply c6, breaking the communication of Black's queen's bishop with the central squares. Such “intermediate" moves, which are made on one's way to solving a particular problem, are of course not detrimental but to the benefit of a thought out plan.
zh: 白象预定的位置是d3，但白方先将军，诱使黑方回应...c6，切断后翼象与中心格的联系。这样在实现某个具体目标途中插入的“过渡着”，当然不会妨碍已经想好的计划，反而有助于实施。

text: If White had not forced the advance ... c6, Black could now, not without advantage, have played 11... Ne4.
zh: 如果白方没有迫使黑方冲起c6，黑方此时便可以有利地走11... Ne4。

text: Of course, if the White bishop were standing not on c1, but on g5, as in Pillsbury's games, his position would be even more threatening. Now Black should think about the defence of the h7 square, since after Qh3 threats begin to hang over him.
zh: 若白象像皮尔斯伯里的对局中那样位于g5，而不是c1，白方的威胁还会更大。不过，即便如此，黑方也必须考虑保护h7，因为Qh3之后他就会面临威胁。

text: In contemplating a complicated regrouping plan, consisting of the transfer of the king’s knight to d6 and the queen’s to f6 which would have given Black control over the e4 point, he overlooks a little combination, as a result of which White wins a pawn.
zh: 阿拉平打算把王翼马调到d6、后翼马调到f6，加强对e4格的控制。然而，他忽略了一个使白方得兵的小组合。

text: Instead of the mistaken retreat of the knight to e8 he should continue 12... Re8 and then... Nf8, defending the main weakness in the castled position - h7. Of course the dominating position of the knight on e5 makes Black's game difficult, but there is a protracted struggle in prospect.
zh: 黑方不应错误地把马退到e8，而应12... Re8再...Nf8，保护王城的主要弱点h7。e5马的强势位置固然使黑方难下，但接下来仍会是一场持久战。

text: **13. Bxh7+ Kxh7 14. Qh3+ Kg8 15. Qxd7 Nd6 16. Qh3 Ne4 17. Rd1 c4**
zh: **13. Bxh7+ Kxh7 14. Qh3+ Kg8 15. Qxd7 Nd6 16. Qh3 Ne4 17. Rd1 c4**

text: A mistaken plan. Locking the centre, in the present position, plays into White's hands and he can now calmly concentrate his efforts on an attack upon the king's flank. He should exchange on c3 and prepare play on the c-file.
zh: 黑方开始执行错误的计划。封闭中心只会帮助白方在王翼进攻；黑方应在c3交换，争取沿c线反击。

text: There is no sense in White taking the pawn on c4 at the cost of a loss of time and removal of the knight from a strong position. On 19. Nxc4 could follow 19... Qc8 20. Qxc8 Rfxc8 21. Ne5 Rc2 or 21... Bd5 and, despite being two pawns down, Black has a strong initiative.
zh: 白方没有必要为了吃c4兵，既损失时间，又让马离开强势位置。19. Nxc4之后可能19... Qc8 20. Qxc8 Rfxc8 21. Ne5 Rc2，或21... Bd5。黑方虽然少两兵，却能取得强大的主动权。

text: Alapin defends himself badly, which, alas, happens with many chessplayers when they get into a difficult position. It was necessary to parry the threat of f6 by 21... f6 (22. Ng6 Re8 23. Qh8+ Kf7) with possibilities of stubborn resistance. Now, however, White obtains a mobile pawn phalanx, crossing the frontier, with which it is difficult to contend. **22. dxe5 f6**
zh:
阿拉平的防守不佳。可惜，许多棋手陷入困境后都会如此。他必须21... f6，防住白方冲起f6的威胁；22. Ng6可用22... Re8 23. Qh8+ Kf7应对，黑方仍能顽强抵抗。现在白方却将形成一支越过中线、能够继续冲击的兵阵，黑方很难应付。

**22. dxe5 f6**

text: To allow f6 would mean being quickly mated.
zh: 若放任白方冲起f6，黑王很快就会被杀。

text: He should decide on 24... a5, and if 25. Bb4 then 25... axb4 26. Rd7 Qxd7 27. exd7 Rad8. **25. Bb4!**

This little combination again escaped Black's orbit of attention. Charousek, in this encounter, showed himself to be far and away more tactically aware than his opponent. The present game well illustrates the significance of tactics in the chess struggle.
zh: 黑方又漏算了一个小组合。恰鲁塞克的战术感觉显然比对手敏锐；即使在这类战略主题鲜明的对局中，战术也起着重要作用。

text: The knight on e5 has made everything “springtime" for White.
zh: e5马使白方全局生机勃勃。

text: Queen's Gambit
zh: 后翼弃兵

text: White: G.Maroczy
zh: 白方：G. 马洛契

text: Black: E.Schiffers
zh: 黑方：E. 希弗斯

text: (Vienna 1898)
**1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. e3 Nbd7 7. Rc1 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5**
zh: **1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. e3 Nbd7 7. Rc1 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Bd3 Bb7 10. O-O c5**

text: All this is known to us from Pillsbury's Hastings games with Tarrasch and Schlechter.
zh: 我们已经熟悉这一局面：皮尔斯伯里在黑斯廷斯对塔拉什和施莱希特时也曾走到这里。

text: In connection with the following move, a manoeuvre which is important for defence of the h7 point. At the same time the rook also “gets to work".
zh: 结合黑方下一步来看，这步棋对保护h7有重要意义，同时也使车更加活跃。

text: The ideal Pillsbury formation. (see next diagram)
zh: 白方形成了理想的皮尔斯伯里式阵势（见下一图）。

text: Black solves a particular problem, striving to close the b1-h7 diagonal and thereby neutralise the influence of the White bishop which is deployed on it.
zh: 黑方只顾解决一个局部问题：封住b1-h7斜线，抵消白象在这条斜线上的作用。

text: Without mentioning the fact that the knight f8 already limits, to a sufficient extent, the action of the bishop b1, Black does not find the planning “core" of the position, which consists of the need to loosen the position of the White knight on e5. If it is conceived that the knight has been driven away from the e5 square, then the weakness of the e3 pawn, located on the open e-file, will be highlighted. Black could then with advantage concentrate the action of his heavy pieces on this line. Consequently, Black's plan must consist of the removal of the White knight from its centralised position. The best attempt in this direction would be the move 13... N6d7. The attack 14. Qh5 is repulsed by the reply 14... g6, while after 14. Bxe7 Qxe7 (or 14... Rxe7) 15. Qg4 f6 16. Nxd7 Nxd7 17. Rce1 Qf7, Black's position is quite satisfactory. Thus 11... Re8 is the beginning of a correct plan of play against the "knight on e5", but with his last move Black misses the right way. **14. Bxe4! dxe4 15. Qb3 Ne6 16. Bxe7 Qxe7 17. d5 c4**
zh:
姑且不说f8马已经足以限制b1象，黑方没有找到制定计划的核心：动摇e5马的位置。假如这只马被赶走，位于开放e线上的e3兵就会显出弱点，黑方便可有利地把重子火力集中到这条线上。因此，黑方的计划必须以驱逐白方中心马为核心。最好的尝试是13... N6d7。14. Qh5可用14... g6击退；14. Bxe7 Qxe7（或14... Rxe7）15. Qg4 f6 16. Nxd7 Nxd7 17. Rce1 Qf7之后，黑方的局面令人满意。由此可见，11... Re8本是正确对抗e5马的计划起点，但黑方上一步偏离了正确方向。

**14. Bxe4! dxe4 15. Qb3 Ne6 16. Bxe7 Qxe7 17. d5 c4**

text: The retreat 17... Nf8 would doom Black to a very cramped position after 18. Rfd1. In order to unravel his forces somewhat, he gives up the c-pawn and he cannot be blamed for this decision. One can only note that such a crucial move as 13... Ne4 needs to be thought out more carefully and made only when it is a link in the plan and not a tactical operation.
zh: 若17... Nf8 18. Rfd1，黑方的局面非常拥挤，因此弃掉c兵不无道理。不过，黑方在走13... Ne4时，就该考虑整个行动计划，而不能只看到眼前的战术效果。

text: He should play 18... Nc5 or 18 Rec8. It turns out that, in sacrificing the pawn, Black again has not assessed the position sufficiently concretely.
zh: 黑方应走18... Nc5或18... Rec8。他弃兵时，显然没有对具体局面作出充分判断。

text: The reader, recalling the principles of planning methods, laid down in the introduction under the sections “Concrete Ideas" and "Dynamics", will undoubtedly accuse Schiffers of insufficiently concrete ideas which led to his serious mistakes on the 13th and 18th moves.
zh: 我们在引言的“具体构想”和“动态性”两节中已经谈到这些问题。黑方第13步和第18步的失误，再次说明了它们的重要性。

text: Thus, again and again, we are convinced of the great significance a concrete approach to positions has in the creative process, i.e. the detailed thinking out of variations, realistic aims and a clear idea of the ways leading to them. Every chess player wishing to cultivate creative thinking must turn his attention to precisely this.
zh: 这再次说明，在创造性的思考过程中，具体地处理局面具有多么重要的意义：仔细推敲变化，设定切合实际的目标，并明确实现目标的途径。每一位希望培养创造性思维的棋手，都应把注意力放在这些方面。

text: White wins two rooks and a knight for the queen. The stage of realisation of this material advantage does not last long, the more so that White also retains a considerably superior position.
zh: 白方以一个后换得双车和一马，取得子力优势；结合原有的局面优势，他很快便能获胜。

text: There is also no comfort in 19... f6 20. Qb3 fxe5 21. f5. **20. exf7+ Kf8**
zh:
19... f6也无济于事，因为20. Qb3 fxe5 21. f5。

**20. exf7+ Kf8**

text: The endgame after 20... Qxf7 21. Nxf7 Kxf7 22. Nb5 Rxc1 23. Rxc1 is hopeless for Black. **21. fxe8=Q+ Kxe8 22. Nxc4 Ba6?**
zh:
20... Qxf7 21. Nxf7 Kxf7 22. Nb5 Rxc1 23. Rxc1之后，黑方的残局无望。

**21. fxe8=Q+ Kxe8 22. Nxc4 Ba6?**

text: Black loses all his bearings and by now does not see “trifles".
zh: 黑方已经乱了方寸，连这些细小的威胁也看不见了。

text: Postponing the denouement for a few moves. 28. Rfc1 or 28. Re7 would have forced immediate resignation. **28... Kg8 29. Rg7+ Kf8 30. Re7 Kg8 31. f7+ Kg7 32. Re8 1-0**
zh:
这只不过把结局推迟了几步。28. Rfc1或28. Re7会迫使黑方立即认输。

**28... Kg8 29. Rg7+ Kf8 30. Re7 Kg8 31. f7+ Kg7 32. Re8 1-0**

text: In the games we have looked at, the positions with the powerful centralised knight arose from one and the same opening - i.e. the Orthodox variation of the Queen's Gambit. In no way does this mean that the same idea cannot be carried out in other opening systems. White's plan includes the move Ne5, as one of its links, also in another branch of the Queen's Gambit, and (albeit more rarely) in other openings. By taking the position of the knight on e5 from the Orthodox Variation, we only wish to demonstrate the role of the knight in the centre with classical examples.
zh: 在上面的例局中，强大的中心马都来自同一种开局：后翼弃兵正统变例。这绝不意味着其他开局体系不能实现同样的构想。在后翼弃兵的其他分支中，甚至在其他开局中，虽然较少见，Ne5也可以成为白方计划的一环。这里选取正统变例的e5马，只是为了用经典例子说明中心马的作用。

text: A comparatively new idea is the deployment of the knight on the central d5 square (d4 for Black). The first plans involving this idea could be seen in games played at the beginning of the 20th century, but the widespread use of it came in the 30's, particularly after it was successfully employed in a number of Botvinnik's games.
zh: 相比之下，以马占据d5（黑方为d4）的构想较晚才受到重视。它在二十世纪初开始出现，到三十年代已被广泛采用；鲍特维尼克尤其擅长运用这一计划。

text: Going back to history, we present two examples in which Black carried out a plan, full of initiative, involving invasion of the knight on d4.
zh: 先看两个较早的例子，说明黑方如何利用d4马。

text: In the game Mieses-Chigorin from the Barmen tournament 1905 (the opening was a Sicilian for White), after 20. Ng1 the struggle arrived at the following position:
zh: 在米泽斯对齐果林一局中（巴门，1905年），双方由反先西西里形成了图示局面。白方刚走完20. Ng1。

text: Black's plan consists of invading with the knight on d4, forcing White to take it, replying... exd4 and then beginning an attack on the e2 pawn along the e-file. This plan was prepared with the advance of the pawns to c5 and e5 and consolidation of them with the moves... b6 and... f6 in case White were to attack the advanced pawns by b4 or f4. It should be noted that this “undermining" - as we call it - move is one of the principal methods against such plans.
zh: 黑方的计划是以马侵入d4，迫使白方吃马，再以...exd4吃回，随后沿e线进攻e2兵。为准备这一计划，黑方先冲起c5、e5，再走...b6和...f6巩固它们，以应对白方通过b4或f4攻击这些已经冲起的兵。应当注意，这类“冲击兵链”的招法，正是对抗此类计划的主要方法之一。

text: The struggle continued:
zh: 实战接着走：

text: The same reply would have also followed on 21. b4.
zh: 对白方的21. b4，黑方也会这样回应。

text: **22. Bxd4 exd4**
zh: **22. Bxd4 exd4**

text: Black threatens to invade the weak e3 square with his knight, via f5.
zh: 现在，黑马准备经f5转到白方的弱格e3。

text: A more consistent way to carry out the plan was 23... Bb3 24. Rd2 Nf5 25. Bxf5 Qxf5 followed by a doubling of rooks on the e-file. This variation was pointed out by Botvinnik, but also the continuation chosen by Chigorin leads to the objective. Black achieved victory on the 42nd move.
zh: 更贯彻计划的下法是23... Bb3 24. Rd2 Nf5 25. Bxf5 Qxf5，再在e线叠车。这一变化由鲍特维尼克指出。不过，齐果林实战所选的后续手段也达到了目的，黑方在第42步获胜。

text: The very complicated position depicted above was obtained in the game Mieses-Billecard, played in the international tournament at Ostende 1907.
zh: 在米泽斯对比耶卡尔一局中（奥斯坦德，1907年），出现了类似的局面。

text: The main difference here is that the White pawn stands not on e2, but on c2 (Mieses exchanged exd5, whereas in the game with Chigorin cxd5) and this difference possibly plays even more into Black's hands.
zh: 主要区别在于，白兵这次不在e2，而在c2：米泽斯先前是exd5，而对齐果林时则是cxd5。这种区别可能更有利于黑方。

text: Without the open c-file, the undermining move b4 loses its strength, indeed it is also more difficult to carry it out.
zh: c线封闭，使白方的b4冲兵既难以实现，效果也较弱。

text: In the game followed
zh: 实战接着走：

text: All White's pieces are crowded in the centre, but he has no apparent objective in view and the harmony of this arrangement is of a purely superficial character.
zh: 白方子力都集中在中心，却找不到攻击目标。这种协调只是表面的。

text: Soon White becomes aware of the futility of “harmony for the sake of harmony".
zh: 这个例子说明，为协调而协调，终究无济于事。

text: He can save the pawn only by 17. Qd2, but also in this case White's position remains difficult.
zh: 只有17. Qd2能够避免丢兵，但白方的局面仍然不好。

text: Of course 17... Nxe3 was also good.
zh: 17... Nxe3也很好。

text: **18. Ne4 Nbxc2 19. Nxc2 Nxc2 20. Qc3 Nd4**
zh: **18. Ne4 Nbxc2 19. Nxc2 Nxc2 20. Qc3 Nd4**

text: It seems only now Mieses saw that on 21. Nxc5 Black replies simply 21... Qc8, creating two threats - to take the knight and... Ne2+.
zh: 米泽斯似乎直到此时才发现，21. Nxc5可用21... Qc8简单应对，同时威胁吃马和...Ne2+。

text: White's position is hopeless, though he dragged on his resistance until the 44th move.
zh: 白方的局面已经无望，不过他坚持到第44步才认输。

text: We look now at what plans, and what techniques of realising them are advanced on this theme in Soviet competitions.
zh: 现在看看苏联赛场上，这一主题又产生了哪些计划及实现计划的方法。

text: English Opening
zh: 英国式开局

text: White: V.Kirillov
zh: 白方：V. 基里洛夫

text: Black: M.Botvinnik
zh: 黑方：M. 鲍特维尼克

text: (7th USSR Championship 1931)
zh: （第七届苏联锦标赛，1931年）

text: Since White has refrained from a quick advance of the queen's pawn to d4, Black first carries out an analogous advance in the centre, possibly already now nurturing a planned thought of invasion with the knight on d4 and a siege of this square on the basis of the two pawn chains a7-b6-c5 and e5-f6-g7.
zh: 白方没有及早将后兵冲起d4，黑方便抢先在中心作了相应的冲兵。他或许此时就在酝酿以马侵入d4的计划，以a7-b6-c5和e5-f6-g7两条兵链为基础，控制这一格。

text: **4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. Bg2 Nc7**
zh: **4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. Bg2 Nc7**

text: This retreat gives away Black's real idea. He actually does intend to carry out the plan, the outline of which was indicated in the previous note.
zh: 这次退马已经显露出黑方的计划。

text: Here 6. d3 is a cunning continuation, intending, on 6... Nc6, to reply 7. Bxc6+! bxc6 8. Qa4 followed by an attack on the c5 pawn by Be3, Ne4, Rc1 etc. Instead of 6... Nc6 Black best stops at 6... g6 and 7... Bg7, continuing to concentrate his attention on the d4 point. **6... Nc6**
zh:
6. d3更灵活。如果6... Nc6，则7. Bxc6+! bxc6 8. Qa4，随后Be3、Ne4和Rc1，可以围攻c5兵。黑方最好以6... g6、7... Bg7回应，把注意力放在d4格上。

**6... Nc6**

text: This position has been met many times and also in recent times.
zh: 实战中经常出现这一局面。

text: White's plan must consist of pressure on the c5 pawn by Na4, Rc1, etc. in order to force... b6 and thereby increase the activity of his king's bishop. **7... e5 8. b3 Be7 9. Bb2 O-O 10. Rc1 f6**
zh:
白方的计划应是以Na4和Rc1向c5施压，迫使黑方走...b6，从而增强g2象的作用。

**7... e5 8. b3 Be7 9. Bb2 O-O 10. Rc1 f6**

text: Exactly the same position occurred in the game Taimanov-Korchnoi, played 23 years later in 1954 in the 21st USSR Championship. **11. Ne1**
zh:
23年后，在1954年第二十一届苏联锦标赛的泰曼诺夫对科尔奇诺伊一局中，又出现了相同局面。

**11. Ne1**

text: This passive retreat would have been justified if White were to include in his plan, as one of the links, the move Bxc6. Taimanov continued 11. Na4 b6 12. Nh4 Nd5 13. a3 (preparing b4) 13... Bb7, and now White should play 13. Nf5 with the threat b4.
zh:
只有把Bxc6作为计划的一环，这种消极退马才有道理。泰曼诺夫走的是11. Na4 b6 12. Nh4 Nd5 13. a3，准备b4，13... Bb7。这时白方应走Nf5，威胁b4。

校勘注：英文原书将此处Nf5的步数印为13；按前文次序应为14，待校对确认。

text: Decisive inattentiveness, which allows Black to completely fulfil the plan of the knight invasion on the main “height" - the d4 point. Necessary was 16. Bxc6 bxc6 17. d3.
zh: 致命的疏忽，使黑马得以侵入d4。白方必须走16. Bxc6 bxc6 17. d3。

text: The weaknesses on the c-file would rather hamper operations, on Black's part, on the king's flank. In any case, it is better to go in for the weakening of his own position, in view of the creation of real weaknesses in the opponent's camp, than to rely only on defence and thereby submit to the will of the opponent and totally hand over the initiative to him.
zh: 黑方在c线一带的弱点，会妨碍他组织王翼行动。与其一味被动等待，不如接受自身的一些弱点，换取对手阵地中切实可攻的弱点。

text: It is difficult for White to find an object for his manoeuvres - the first sign that the opponent has seized the initiative.
zh: 白方很难为子力调动找到目标，这是对手已经夺得主动权的第一个征兆。

text: The plan is fulfilled and now comes the concluding stage to realise the positional advantage.
zh: 黑方已经完成计划，现在进入最后阶段：兑现所取得的局面优势。

text: Botvinnik assessed the present position like this: “Black has achieved ideal positions for his pieces and pawns. His knights cannot be attacked, since the moves a3 and e3 would only ruin White's position." **22. Nf3?**
zh:
鲍特维尼克这样评价当前局面：“黑方子力与兵的位置已经达到理想状态。白方无法攻击黑马，因为a3和e3都只会破坏自己的局面。”

**22. Nf3?**

text: Leading to a quick defeat, but also after 22. a3 Nbc6 23. e3 Nf5 24. Bf1 Na5 White must perish sooner or later. There is the threat if only of the manoeuvre... Qe8-f7. **22... Nxa2! 23. Nxd4 Nxc3 24. Rxc3 cxd4 25. Rxc8 Rxc8 26. e3 Bb4 27. Re2 Bc3 28. exd4 Bxb2 29. Rxb2 Qxd4 30. Ra2 a5 31. Ra4 Qc3 32. Rh4 Qc1 0-1**
zh:
这步棋导致速败，但即便22. a3 Nbc6 23. e3 Nf5 24. Bf1 Na5，白方迟早也难逃败局。黑方仅以...Qe8-f7调后就能制造威胁。

**22... Nxa2! 23. Nxd4 Nxc3 24. Rxc3 cxd4 25. Rxc8 Rxc8 26. e3 Bb4 27. Re2 Bc3 28. exd4 Bxb2 29. Rxb2 Qxd4 30. Ra2 a5 31. Ra4 Qc3 32. Rh4 Qc1 0-1**

text: Sicilian Defence
zh: 西西里防御

text: White: G.Levenfish
zh: 白方：G. 列文菲什

text: Black: G.Lisitsin
zh: 黑方：G. 利西岑

text: (Moscow 1935)
Black leads the game into one of the set-ups of the Sicilian Defence called the “Dragon Variation" (the pawn configuration resembles the position of the stars in the Dragon constellation).
zh: 黑方将对局引入西西里防御的一种阵势，称为“龙式变例”（其兵形类似天龙座的星位排列）。

text: In the usual form of this variation, White's pawn is still on c2, but even in this case Black strives for the move... d5, relieving the situation around the d5 point, the pressure on which by White, is felt very strongly even without the pawn on c4. All the more reason why Black, instead of a stereotyped arrangement of pieces and pawns, should play... d5.
zh: 在这个变例的通常形态中，白方的c兵还留在c2。即使没有c4兵，白方对d5格的压力也已经很强，黑方仍须争取...d5，缓解这一带的紧张。既然本局白兵已在c4，黑方就更不应机械地布置子力和兵，而应设法冲起d5。

text: White outstrips Black in the clash over the central squares. From this moment, the game becomes surprisingly similar to the game Kirillov-Botvinnik, the only difference being that Levenfish now carries out Botvinnik's plan with White, while Lisitsin repeats Kirillov's method of defence with Black.
zh: 白方在中心格的争夺中抢先一步。从这里开始，本局与基里洛夫对鲍特维尼克一局惊人地相似，只不过这次是执白的列文菲什实施鲍特维尼克的计划，而执黑的利西岑重复基里洛夫的防守方式。

text: White now plays directly for the setting up of a cavalry outpost on d5.
zh: 白方随即着手在d5建立马的前哨据点。

text: Also here it was still possible to complicate White's task by 4... Bg7 5. dxc5 Qa5. However, neither here nor later, does Black prevent the opponent from placing his forces “a la Botvinnik".
zh: 黑方此时仍可用4... Bg7 5. dxc5 Qa5增加白方的困难。但无论现在还是以后，黑方都没有阻止对手按照“鲍特维尼克的方式”布置子力。

text: **5. Nxd4 Bg7 6. e4 d6 7. Be2 O-O 8. O-O Nbd7 9. Be3 Nc5 10. f3 b6 11. Qd2 Bb7 12. Rfd1 Ne6 13. Rac1 Qd7 14. Ndb5 Ne8 15. Nd5**
zh: **5. Nxd4 Bg7 6. e4 d6 7. Be2 O-O 8. O-O Nbd7 9. Be3 Nc5 10. f3 b6 11. Qd2 Bb7 12. Rfd1 Ne6 13. Rac1 Qd7 14. Ndb5 Ne8 15. Nd5**

text: It is necessary to look now at the position occurring after the 21st move in the game Kirillov-Botvinnik. White's arrangement of pieces and pawns is very similar in both cases, only Botvinnik's b-pawn was advanced to b6, whereas Levenfish's is still on its original square.
zh: 请回看基里洛夫对鲍特维尼克一局第21步后的局面。两局进攻方的子力与兵配置非常相似，只是鲍特维尼克的b兵已经冲起b6，而列文菲什的b兵仍在初始格。

text: It is interesting that Levenfish achieves this type of piece arrangement already on the 16th move, while Botvinnik only on the 22nd move. This is explained by the fact that Botvinnik's queen got to d7 in three moves, Levenfish's to d2 - in one move; Botvinnik's knight transferred from g8 to b4 in five moves, Levenfish's from g1 to b5 in three; finally Botvinnik's bishop reached the e6 square in two steps, Levenfish's e3 - in one.
zh: 有意思的是，列文菲什在第16步时便达到这种阵势，鲍特维尼克却到第22步才做到。原因在于：鲍特维尼克的后走了三步才到d7，列文菲什的后一步就到d2；鲍特维尼克的马从g8到b4用了五步，列文菲什的马从g1到b5只用了三步；最后，鲍特维尼克的象用了两步到e6，列文菲什的象一步便到e3。

text: Curiously, these six moves for Kirillov have been wasted for nothing. It is clear why Levenfish's position is more capable of defence than Kirillov's position. Thus many chessplayers unwittingly squander an important element of the struggle - time - in vain. Make the most of time - this legacy of Morphy, Chigorin, Alekhine must be placed at the basis of enterprising chess thoughts.
zh:
奇怪的是，基里洛夫多得到的这六步竟然白白浪费了。这就解释了为什么利西岑的局面比基里洛夫的局面更容易防守。许多棋手往往在不知不觉中浪费了斗争中的重要因素——时间。充分利用时间，是墨菲、齐果林和阿廖欣留给我们的宝贵经验，必须成为积极思考棋局的基础。

校勘注：本段英文原书印作“Levenfish’s position”，但根据前后两局攻守双方的对应关系，此处应指防守方利西岑，译文据此订正。

text: Under the cover of his threateningly placed knight on d5, White intends to launch an attack by f4-f5 or f4 and then e5. It is dangerous for Black to stick to waiting tactics, and he decides to take the knight d5, though this also leads to the creation of new weaknesses in his camp. **16... Nxd5 17. cxd5 Nc7 18. a4 Ba6**
zh:
在具有威慑力的d5马掩护下，白方准备以f4-f5，或先f4再e5发动进攻。黑方若继续等待将十分危险，因此决定交换d5马，尽管这也会在自身阵地中造成新的弱点。

**16... Nxd5 17. cxd5 Nc7 18. a4 Ba6**

text: A positionally unjustified exchange, which decisively weakens the c6 square, where White's pieces will soon also be heading. Generally speaking, it is necessary for Black to hold on more actively, otherwise, little by little, White will simply run all over him. He should contemplate formulating a plan which entails the break... f5 or the advance of the e-pawn.
zh: 这次兑象在局面上没有依据，反而严重削弱了c6格，白方子力很快就会向那里集结。总体而言，黑方必须更积极地应战，否则白方会逐步将他压垮。他应考虑以...f5冲兵突破，或冲起e兵，制定相应的行动计划。

text: **19. b4 Bxe2 20. Nxe2 Na6 21. Nd4 Bxd4**
zh: **19. b4 Bxe2 20. Nxe2 Na6 21. Nd4 Bxd4**

text: It is painful to make such an exchange, but he cannot allow the knight to c6. However, even now it is not very nice: on c6 is not a gaping hole, but a real abyss.
zh: 这样兑换令人难受，但黑方又不能容许白马进入c6。然而，即便兑了马，局面也好不到哪里去：c6已不仅是一个漏洞，简直成了深渊。

text: Threatening Bh6.
zh: 威胁Bh6。

text: The problem is solved. Black cannot allow the capture of the c-file and is forced to exchange on c6. Thus the modest pawn on c2, beginning its procession with the first move, after a little diversion gets to c6 and sticks like a bayonet into the heart of the opponent.
zh: 问题解决了。黑方不能容许白方占据c线，只能在c6交换。于是，那只从c2出发、第一步便投入战斗的小兵，稍经迂回就到达c6，像刺刀一样直插对手的心脏。

text: It is not difficult to see that the passed pawn on c6 has been created as a result of the knight invasion on d5.
zh: 不难看出，c6通路兵正是白马侵入d5所带来的成果。

text: Transferring from stage to stage, White's plan now approaches the area of realisation of the advantage which has been achieved.
zh: 白方的计划环环相扣，现在已经进入兑现优势的阶段。

text: **25. Qc3 Nc7 26. Ra1 Rc8 27. Qd3 d5 28. Rc1 f5 29. Bf4! dxe4 30. fxe4 Ne8**
zh: **25. Qc3 Nc7 26. Ra1 Rc8 27. Qd3 d5 28. Rc1 f5 29. Bf4! dxe4 30. fxe4 Ne8**

text: It turns out that, after 30... fxe4, White wins the knight by 31. Qd7. Also miserable is 30... Qxe4, because of the same 31. Qd7. All this - is a consequence of the menacing pawn on c6, which deprives the opponent of sufficient freedom of activity.
zh: 原来，30... fxe4会遭到31. Qd7，白方得马。30... Qxe4同样糟糕，白方仍走31. Qd7。这一切都源于c6兵的强大威力：它严重限制了黑方的活动自由。

text: **31. exf5 gxf5 32. b5 Kf7 33. Rf1 Ng7 34. Bd2 Rf8 35. Re1 Qc8 36. Bb4 Re8**
zh: **31. exf5 gxf5 32. b5 Kf7 33. Rf1 Ng7 34. Bd2 Rf8 35. Re1 Qc8 36. Bb4 Re8**

text: The Black pieces are constrained and White must gain victory without difficulty. However, at this moment, he mistakenly, apparently under the influence of time-trouble (in the 2nd Moscow international tournament the control was 2½ hours for the first 37 moves), transposed to the endgame by
zh: 黑方子力受到束缚，白方本应轻松获胜。但白方此时却错误地转入残局，看来是受到时间紧张的影响。这届第二次莫斯科国际大赛的时限，是两个半小时走完前37步。

text: 37. Qd4, with the threats of Bxe7 and Bc3, led to victory. On the best 37... Qc7 would have followed 38. Bc3 Ne6 39. Qd5, or 38... Nh5 39. Qh4, or, finally, 38... Rg8 39. Qc4+ Kf8 40. Bb4.
zh: 37. Qd4可获胜，同时威胁Bxe7和Bc3。对最好的37... Qc7，白方可走38. Bc3 Ne6 39. Qd5；若38... Nh5，则39. Qh4；若38... Rg8，则39. Qc4+ Kf8 40. Bb4。

text: After the transposition to the ending **37... Qxd7 38. cxd7 Rd8 39. Rxe7+** the game loses interest for our theme. Lisitsin put up further quite stubborn resistance and laid down his arms only on the 62nd move.
zh:
实战转入残局：

**37... Qxd7 38. cxd7 Rd8 39. Rxe7+**

此后的进程与本节主题已无直接关系。利西岑继续顽强抵抗，直到第62步才认输。

text: We look at one more game, brilliantly illustrating the role of the centralised knight on d5.
zh: 再看一盘精彩例局，进一步说明中心d5马的作用。

text: Reti Opening
zh: 列蒂开局

text: White: M.Botvinnik
zh: 白方：M. 鲍特维尼克

text: Black: A.Lilienthal
zh: 黑方：A. 利林塔尔

text: (Moscow 1936)

A good plan, also frequently employed with success in the international tournament at Marienbad (Marianske-Lazne) 1925. By crossing the centre with the two bishops, Black threatens to obtain predominant influence over it. This forces White to submit to the exchange of the white-squared bishops, which leads to a slight weakening of his castled position.
zh: 这是一个好计划，1925年马里恩巴德（玛丽亚温泉市）国际大赛中也曾多次成功采用。黑方让双象交叉瞄准中心，力图取得对中心的主导权。白方因此不得不接受白格象的交换，使易位后的王城略为削弱。

text: **6. d4 cxd4 7. Nxd4 Bxg2 8. Kxg2 Bg7 9. Nc3**
zh: **6. d4 cxd4 7. Nxd4 Bxg2 8. Kxg2 Bg7 9. Nc3**

text: White intends to play e4 in order to occupy the d5 square.
zh: 白方准备冲起e4，以便占据d5格。

text: Black ignores the opponent's plan, which bears witness to his insufficiently concrete assessment of the position.
zh: 黑方无视对手的计划，说明他对局面的判断还不够具体。

text: 2½ months later, the same position was met in the international tournament at Nottingham, in the game Capablanca-Botvinnik. The latter played 9... Qc8, attacking the c4 pawn. There followed 10. b3 Qb7+ 11. f3 d5 12. cxd5 Nxd5 13. Nxd5 Qxd5 14. Bb2 O-O 15. Qd3 Rfd8 16. Rfd1 Nd7 and a draw was agreed on the 29th move. **10. e4!**
zh:
两个半月后，诺丁汉国际大赛的卡帕布兰卡对鲍特维尼克一局也出现了相同局面。鲍特维尼克走9... Qc8，攻击c4兵。随后是10. b3 Qb7+ 11. f3 d5 12. cxd5 Nxd5 13. Nxd5 Qxd5 14. Bb2 O-O 15. Qd3 Rfd8 16. Rfd1 Nd7，双方在第29步同意和棋。

**10. e4!**

text: White immediately exploits the opponent's routine play (with his last move, Black “completed" his development). The plan of the knight invasion on d5 really takes shape.
zh: 白方立即利用了对手的机械下法——黑方上一步只是照例“完成”出子。白马侵入d5的计划开始具体成形。

text: Preparing ... b5, in order to rather weaken White's pressure on the “critical" (the object of the plan) d5 point and, by opening the c-file, to begin a clash of heavy pieces on it, which would give new direction to the struggle.
zh: 准备...b5，减轻白方对计划关键目标d5格的压力，同时打开c线，让双方重子在该线展开交锋，使斗争转向新的方向。

text: Black's concrete idea consists of the variation 16... Nxd4 17. Bxd4 b5, but even in this case he would run into difficulties after 18. Bxf6 and 19. Nd5 with the threat e5. Therefore Black would have to look for some sort of prophylactic move before deciding on... b5, but this would also have allowed White to take appropriate measures against the advance of the b-pawn.
zh: 黑方的具体构想是16... Nxd4 17. Bxd4 b5。但即使如此，18. Bxf6接19. Nd5、威胁e5，也会使黑方陷入困难。因此，在决定冲起b5之前，黑方必须先作某种预防；然而这也会给白方时间，采取相应措施阻止b兵冲起。

text: **16. Rfd1 Nxd4 17. Bxd4 d6**
zh: **16. Rfd1 Nxd4 17. Bxd4 d6**

text: Black has a difficult position.
zh: 黑方的局面很难下。

text: An immediate... b5, as indicated earlier, is dangerous. It was possible to take the d5 square under control by the move... e6, but after 18. a4 Black would again find himself in a blind alley, since, as it is not difficult to see, 18... d5 leads to the loss of a pawn, while the f6 and d6 points serve as new objects for attack.
zh: 如前所述，立即...b5很危险。黑方本可用...e6控制d5，但18. a4之后又会陷入困境：不难看出，18... d5会丢兵，而f6和d6又会成为新的攻击目标。

text: Black's plan is not very clear. You see, the exchange of bishops only increases White's chances on the king's flank. Besides this, the knight is, as it were, excluded from events on the queen's flank. Undoubtedly more active was 18... Nd7. The Black knight, reaching c5, would fulfil the functions of both attack and defence. Finally, also possible was the tactical plan with 18... h5, and if 19. Nd5 then 19... Nxd5 20. exd5 e5 21. dxe6 fxe6, and the game is sharpened, in view of the possibilities on the f-file. Now, however, Black finally concedes the d5 square to the White knight. **19. Nd5 Rc6 20. Bxg7 Nxg7**
zh:
黑方的计划不够明确。交换双象只会增加白方在王翼的机会，而马退到e8后，也几乎退出了后翼的战斗。18... Nd7显然更积极：黑马到达c5后，可以兼顾攻守。此外，还可考虑以18... h5为起点的战术计划；若19. Nd5，则19... Nxd5 20. exd5 e5 21. dxe6 fxe6，黑方在f线上的机会将使局面趋于尖锐。而实战中，黑方终于把d5格彻底让给了白马。

**19. Nd5 Rc6 20. Bxg7 Nxg7**

text: White has fulfilled the basic part of the plan: to invade with the knight on d5 and secure, more or less firmly, this central position for it. Can one say that he has achieved a positional advantage? Of course!
zh: 白方已经完成计划的基本部分：以马侵入d5，并使它在中心大体站稳。能否说白方已经取得局面优势？当然可以！

text: Already in a number of examples, we have been convinced of the significance of the knight, if it is firmly established in the centre. At the same time, the invasion of the knight on d5 - is not an end in itself, but only an important step in the concluding stage of the plan - the realisation of the advantage which has been achieved.
zh: 前面的多个例子已经说明，一只稳据中心的马具有多么重要的作用。不过，马侵入d5并不是最终目的，而只是通向计划最后阶段——兑现既得优势——的重要一步。

text: Thus, White is now posed with the question: how can he exploit the strong position of the knight? It is not apparent what operation White can undertake on the queen's flank under the aegis of the knight on d5. Here White should only be watchful that Black does not “on the sly" carry out the break... b5. Obviously, White has the better chances on the king's flank or in the centre, in connection with the possible opening of the c-file.
zh: 白方面临的新问题是：怎样利用马的强势位置？在d5马的掩护下，白方似乎没有合适的后翼行动可做；在这一翼，他只需留意，不能让黑方悄悄实现...b5冲兵突破。显然，白方在王翼的机会更多，也可以结合打开c线的可能性，在中心寻求进展。

text: It is interesting that the move 21. e5 is possible at once. Black cannot take the pawn in view of Nxe7+ or Nf6+. The best, if not the only defence was 21... Ne6. Further events could develop like this: 22. Re1 dxe5 23. Rxe5 Rcd6 24. Qh6 b5, and, little by little, counter chances are created for Black. White plays in a more subtle way. He strives to rivet the knight to the g7 square.
zh: 有意思的是，白方现在就可以走21. e5。由于Nxe7+或Nf6+的威胁，黑方不能吃兵。21... Ne6是最好的防守，甚至可能是唯一的防守。此后可能走22. Re1 dxe5 23. Rxe5 Rcd6 24. Qh6 b5，黑方便逐渐获得反击机会。白方选择了更细腻的下法，力图把黑马拴在g7。

text: Now, on the removal of the knight to e8 or e6, follows h5.
zh: 现在，黑马若转到e8或e6，白方就冲起h5。

text: Black defends against the threat e5, which, after the move 21. h4, gains still more in strength. Now it is necessary for White to once again exploit the advantage of his position. **22. Rc3 Nh5**
zh:
黑方防住了e5的威胁；白方走过21. h4之后，这步冲兵的威力已经更强。现在白方必须重新寻找利用局面优势的方法。

**22. Rc3 Nh5**

text: Probably intending, even if at the cost of a significant weakening of the pawn chain, to remove White's central knight after... Nf6.
zh: 黑方大概准备走...Nf6，交换白方的中心马，即使为此严重削弱兵链也在所不惜。

text: He should continue 23. Rd3, to prevent the move... Nf6.
zh: 白方应走23. Rd3，阻止...Nf6。

text: A mistake. It was possible to play 23... Nf6, because the variation 24. Nxf6+ exf6 25. Qxf6 is unfavourable for White in view of 25... d5! On 23... Nf6, correct is 24. Rfc1 or 24. Re1, and, as before, the move... b5 is not possible.
zh: 错误。黑方本可走23... Nf6，因为24. Nxf6+ exf6 25. Qxf6 d5!这一变化对白方不利。对23... Nf6，白方应走24. Rfc1或24. Re1；这样，黑方仍然不能冲起b5。

text: Now, however, White, having created a positional advantage, further achieves also a material superiority. The reason why Black decides to prematurely provoke a crisis in the struggle lies apparently in psychological instability, which is evoked by the difficulties of a protracted defence.
zh: 现在白方在局面优势之外，又将取得子力优势。黑方过早将斗争推向决战，原因看来在于长期艰苦防守所带来的心理动摇。

text: **24. cxb5 axb5 25. Rdc1! Rxc3 26. Rxc3 bxa4** If 26... e6, White has 27. Rc7 followed by Ne7+.
zh:
**24. cxb5 axb5 25. Rdc1! Rxc3 26. Rxc3 bxa4**

若26... e6，则27. Rc7，随后Ne7+。

text: White prefers to transpose play into the endgame, which is won comparatively easily, rather than trouble himself with worries about the opponent's passed pawn after 28. Nxe7+ Rxe7 29. Rxe7 axb3. However, the Black king and knight are so badly placed that even here the way to the win would be quick and uncomplicated, for example 30. Rc7!, threatening not only mate, but also Qb2 followed by Rc3. If 30... Qe2+, then 31. Qf2, and the b3 pawn is lost. On 30... Qb8, decisive is 31. Qc3. **28... Qe2+ 29. Qf2 Qxf2+ 30. Kxf2 e6 31. Nb6**... (1-0, 44)
zh:
白方宁愿转入较易取胜的残局，也不愿在28. Nxe7+ Rxe7 29. Rxe7 axb3之后，为对手的通路兵操心。不过，即便走这一变化，黑王和黑马的位置也实在太差，白方仍可简单迅速地取胜。例如30. Rc7!，不仅威胁将杀，还威胁Qb2接Rc3。若30... Qe2+，则31. Qf2，b3兵将被吃掉；若30... Qb8，则31. Qc3决定胜负。

**28... Qe2+ 29. Qf2 Qxf2+ 30. Kxf2 e6 31. Nb6**

白方第44步获胜。

text: We have convinced ourselves, by a number of examples, what a powerful positional role the knight plays when it is established on one of the central squares.
zh: 通过这些例子，我们已经看到：马一旦在中心格站稳，就能发挥强大的局面作用。

text: However, the theme "knight in the centre" represents only a part, and besides not the main, problem of the centre as a whole. Principal consideration in a set plan needs to be given to the question of pawn play in the centre.
zh: 不过，“中心马”只是整个中心问题的一部分，而且并非最主要的部分。制定计划时，更应着重考虑如何在中心运用兵。

text: Even in the last century, the stars of the epoch, with Steinitz atheir head, formulated the most important positional concept "the pawn centre" and revealed its enormous significance when carrying out active plans in the central stage of the game.
zh: 早在十九世纪，以斯坦尼茨为首的名家就提出了一个极为重要的局面概念——“兵中心”，并揭示出它对于在中局实施积极计划的巨大意义。

text: Pawns placed on the central squares e4, d4 (e5, d5) are called the pawn centre.
zh: 位于中心格e4、d4（黑方为e5、d5）的兵，构成兵中心。

text: Two central pawns, standing side by side, hold under their influence four squares on the next rank. Thus the presence of the pawn centre for one of the sides predetermines a certain territorial achievement, which to some extent hampers the opponent, while in specific conditions might serve as a guarantee for a threatening attack. The advance of the pawn centre sometimes causes real disarray in the enemy camp, particularly when a counterattack against such a breakthrough group proves unsuccessful. The pawn centre gains in strength when there is harmony between it and the piece forces. If pawn support is required to consolidate a knight in the centre, then here the pawns need the support of pieces.
zh: 两个并列的中心兵可以控制前一横线上的四个格。因此，一方拥有兵中心，就意味着取得了一定的空间优势，能够在某种程度上限制对手；在适当条件下，它还可成为发动强大攻势的保障。中心兵向前冲击，有时会使敌阵陷入混乱，尤其是在对手反击这支突破力量未能奏效时。兵中心与其他子力协调配合，才能充分发挥威力。中心马需要兵的保护才能站稳；同样，中心兵也需要棋子的支持。

text: When the pawn centre advances, it loses touch with its own rear and draws closer to the superior strength of the opponent. Therefore an attacking march of the central pawns - is a highly responsible operation, which must be weighed up as accurately and deeply as possible. Failure, usually taking the form of an annihilation of the breakthrough group, is virtually equivalent to defeat. On the other hand, success, for the most part, guarantees victory.
zh: 中心兵向前冲击时，会逐渐远离己方后援，接近对手兵力占优的区域。因此，以中心兵发动进攻是一项关系重大的行动，必须尽可能准确、深入地权衡。一旦失败，突破兵群通常会被消灭，这几乎等于输棋；反之，若能成功，往往也就胜券在握。

text: A good illustration of the strength and weakness of the pawn centre, breaking through, is served by the following variation of the Alekhine Defence:
zh: 阿廖欣防御的下列变化，可以很好地说明向前突破的兵中心所具有的强点与弱点：

text: Black agrees to delay his development, but in return induces the White pawns to lose touch with their forces, considerably weakening the central squares in their camp and exposing the position of the White king.
zh: 黑方甘愿暂缓出子，诱使白兵远离己方子力，严重削弱白方阵营中的中心格，同时使白王的位置暴露。

text: If the White pawn were standing on e4, his pawn centre would be stronger and Black's position cramped. From this it is seen how a pawn advance contains a positional minus.
zh: 如果白方的e兵仍在e4，他的兵中心就会更强，黑方也会更受束缚。由此可见，冲兵也有其局面上的代价。

text: Consistent, but exposing the White king even more and weakening the e3 and e4 squares in the centre. In return, White's central pawn chain spreads its influence over many squares in the opponent's territory. If he succeeds in maintaining the pawn centre and completing his development, then he will achieve an overwhelming advantage, but Black quickly organises an attack on the weak pawns and the struggle assumes an extremely sharp character.
zh: 这步棋贯彻了白方的构想，但进一步暴露了白王，并削弱中心的e3、e4两格。作为补偿，白方中心兵链把控制范围扩展到对手阵地中的许多格。只要白方能保住兵中心并完成出子，就会取得压倒性优势；然而黑方迅速组织对弱兵的攻击，使斗争变得极为尖锐。

text: Black himself forces the opponent's central pawns to advance. 6... Bf5 is a well-analysed theoretical continuation, but in precisely this case White succeeds in stabilising the position with his pawn group in the centre, and Black has to manoeuvre for a long time in very restricted space. This makes it very difficult for him to plan his game.
zh: 黑方主动迫使对手的中心兵继续前冲。6... Bf5是一个经过充分研究的理论后续手段，但这样白方反而能巩固中心兵群，黑方则必须长期在非常狭窄的空间内调动子力，难以制定行棋计划。

text: 8. d6 is unsatisfactory, if only because of 8... Qh4+.
zh: 8. d6不好，黑方仅以8... Qh4+应对就足够了。

text: White's pawn centre has shifted to the fifth rank and continues to remain mobile. However, in a number of games, Black managed to avert the danger which might hang over his king.
zh: 白方的兵中心已移到第五横线，而且仍能继续冲起。不过，在一些实战中，黑方成功化解了可能威胁到王的危险。

text: Black has surrounded and attacked White's pawns which are breaking through. The tension of the struggle has reached its height.
zh: 黑方已经包围并攻击白方试图突破的中心兵，斗争的紧张程度达到顶点。

text: He could fight on by 11... Kd8 12. Bg5+ Be7. **12. Qe2!**
zh:
11... Kd8 12. Bg5+ Be7还可以继续战斗。

**12. Qe2!**

text: The best and probably a winning continuation of the attack. In a few games White played 12. Bxd7+? and... lost because of the weakness of the pawns.
zh: 这是继续进攻的最佳手段，很可能已经足以获胜。有些实战中，白方走12. Bxd7+?，结果反而因兵的弱点而输棋。

text: White's last move seemed to be bad precisely because of this capture. We mention, incidentally, that 12... a6 is not good because of 13. e6 Bxb5 14. exf7+ Kd8 15. Bg5+ Kc7 16. Nxb5+ axb5 17. Bf4+. **13. e6!**
zh:
正因为黑方可以这样吃兵，白方上一步看起来似乎不好。顺便指出，12... a6也不行，因为13. e6 Bxb5 14. exf7+ Kd8 15. Bg5+ Kc7 16. Nxb5+ axb5 17. Bf4+。

**13. e6!**

text: Now Black's position caves in.
zh: 黑方的局面就此崩溃。

text: And White's attack after 15... Qxb2 16. exf7+ Kxf7 17. Qh5+ is irresistible.
zh: 15... Qxb2 16. exf7+ Kxf7 17. Qh5+之后，白方的攻势势不可挡。

text: Already from what has been said it is clear that the plan of struggle against the pawn centre is broken down into two stages: slowing down the advance of the centre, and then, after solving the first problem, organising an attack on it. It is appropriate to mention that, with such a blockaded centre, the game might be carried over also to the flanks. However, it is best not to allow the opponent to create a pawn centre, particularly when it is located on the open files.
zh: 由以上讨论已经可以看出，对抗兵中心的计划分为两个阶段：先遏制中心兵的冲击，再组织力量攻击它们。值得一提的是，中心一旦被封锁，战斗也可能转移到两翼。不过，最好还是不让对手建立兵中心，尤其要防止其在开放线上形成。

text: The pawn centre is such a major positional factor that, because of it, the struggle commences already with the first opening moves.
zh: 兵中心是如此重要的局面因素，以至于围绕它的争夺从开局第一步便已开始。

text: Usually the side enjoying the initiative in this struggle is White, since, already with his first moves, he can maintain one of his pawns in the centre. The strategy of Black's opening plan is, for the most part, directed towards the establishment of pawn equilibrium in the centre. Therefore the creation of a pawn centre is a very complicated operation for White, if Black watches his opening moves closely. This occurs in the French Defence (1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 and already there is equilibrium), the Sicilian Defence (1. e4 c5, preventing the move d4; if now 2. c3, then 2... Nf6 or 2... d5, decisively obstructing White's plan), the Nimzovich Defence (1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4, and Black succeeds in preventing the formation of White pawns in the centre; he still has the move... d5 in reserve) and many other openings.
zh: 白方通常在这场争夺中占据主动，因为他从最初几步起就能以兵占住中心。黑方开局计划的战略重点，大多是建立中心兵的均衡。因此，只要黑方在开局谨慎行棋，白方要建立兵中心就会相当困难。法兰西防御便是如此：1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5，中心已经形成均衡。西西里防御也是如此：1. e4 c5，阻止白方冲起d4；若2. c3，则2... Nf6或2... d5，有力阻碍白方的计划。尼姆佐-印度防御中，1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4，黑方同样能阻止白方形成兵中心，而且还保留着...d5的选择。许多其他开局也有类似情况。

text: And yet White (and at other times also Black!) sometimes succeeds in creating a pawn centre as a result of the opening struggle. Here are a few examples. Queen's Gambit Accepted
zh:
尽管如此，白方——有时也包括黑方！——仍可能在开局争夺后成功建立兵中心。下面看几个例子。

后翼弃兵接受式

text: White: M.Botvinnik
zh: 白方：M. 鲍特维尼克

text: Black: G.Levenfish
zh: 黑方：G. 列文菲什

text: (Moscow 1935)

Black has the possibility of transferring to the central stage with a more or less reasonable game, but he requires an excellent understanding of the problems facing him. The fact of the matter is that, after the removal of the Black pawn from d5, White threatens to build up a pawn centre. S. Tarrasch even considered the move 2... dxc4 to be a surrender of the centre and invariably gave it a question mark. This evaluation, however, is dogmatic. Black has quite a few ways of preventing the advance e4, indeed the position of the d4 pawn is also not absolutely stable, in view of the possible breaks... c5 and... e5. Of course the replies 2... c6 or 2... e6, consolidating the d5 pawn, facilitate Black's struggle in the centre, but lead to a comparatively quiet game in which it is difficult for him to obtain counterattacking chances. The move 2... dxc4, however, allows a sharpening of the struggle. In the tense situation created after accepting the gambit, Black can exploit a number of combinational motifs. Thus if White now plays directly for the pawn centre 3. e4, then he obtains nothing in view of the reply 3... e5 (4. dxe5 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 Be6 and then... Nc6 with hopes of seizing the initiative). On 3. Nc3, in the game Capablanca-I. Rabinovich (Moscow 1925) Black replied 3... a6 and after 4. a4 e5! obtained a position with excellent prospects. **3. Nf3 Nf6**
zh:
黑方可以带着大体合理的局面进入中局，但必须充分理解自己面临的问题。d5兵离开中心后，白方便有建立兵中心的可能。塔拉什甚至认为2... dxc4是在放弃中心，总给这步棋打上问号。然而，这种评价过于教条。黑方有不少方法阻止e4；而由于...c5和...e5冲兵突破的可能性，白方d4兵的位置也并非绝对稳固。当然，2... c6或2... e6巩固d5兵，更便于黑方争夺中心，但局势相对平静，黑方不易获得反击机会。2... dxc4则能使斗争更加尖锐。在接受弃兵后形成的紧张局面中，黑方可以利用多种战术因素。例如，白方若立即以3. e4建立兵中心，黑方可用3... e5回应；4. dxe5 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 Be6，随后...Nc6，黑方有望夺得主动，白方并无所获。对3. Nc3，卡帕布兰卡对I. 拉比诺维奇一局（莫斯科，1925年）中，黑方以3... a6回应，4. a4 e5!之后取得了前景极佳的局面。

**3. Nf3 Nf6**

text: Beginning the struggle around the move e4.
zh: 双方开始围绕e4的可能性展开争夺。

text: By threatening to defend the pawn by... b5, Black forces his opponent to spend time on capturing the pawn. If 4... Nbd7, then 5. Nc3 and the move e4 cannot be prevented.
zh: 黑方威胁以...b5保兵，迫使白方花时间吃回这只兵。若4... Nbd7，则5. Nc3，白方的e4已无法阻止。

text: **5. Qxc4 Bf5! 6. Nc3 Nbd7 7. g3 Ne4 8. Bg2 Nd6**
zh: **5. Qxc4 Bf5! 6. Nc3 Nbd7 7. g3 Ne4 8. Bg2 Nd6**

text: A tempting decision, but now the struggle against e4 is made difficult. On 8... Ndf6 would have followed 9. Ne5, and White once again draws closer to the cherished advance of the e-pawn. Black could have put up a more successful resistance by 8... Nxc3 9. bxc3 Be4.
zh: 一个诱人的选择，却增加了阻止e4的难度。如果8... Ndf6，则9. Ne5，白方又更接近期待已久的e兵冲起。黑方用8... Nxc3 9. bxc3 Be4可以进行更有效的抵抗。

text: At last!
zh: 终于实现了！

text: Black's position is not easy. White has built up a pawn centre and a mobile one at that, as a consequence of which his piece army also threatens to advance. Black lags behind seriously in development (this is also not surprising, since, out of his first ten moves, he has made five with the knight), his king is detained in the centre - it all foreshadows an impending denouement.
zh: 黑方的局面很难下。白方不仅建立了兵中心，而且中心兵还可以继续冲起，其他子力也有随之压上的可能。黑方出子严重落后——前十步中有五步都在动马，这也就不足为奇了——王仍滞留中心。这一切都预示着决战即将到来。

text: The question, as to whether he should hurry with the opening of the game or continue to systematically increase the pressure resulting from the pawn centre, presents itself a purely strategical problem. Both plans are justified and the choice of one of them, in the present position, depends more on the style and creative direction of the chessplayer.
zh: 是立即打开局面，还是继续依托兵中心，有条不紊地增加压力？这是一个纯粹的战略问题。两种计划都有道理。在当前局面下，选择哪一种，更多取决于棋手的风格和创作倾向。

text: And White's advantage is quite obvious. Admittedly, the process of realisation still requires quite a long time.
zh: 白方的优势已经十分明显，不过兑现优势仍需相当长的时间。

text: A brilliant illustration of the influence of the pawn centre upon the whole area of the struggle is provided by the following game:
zh: 下面这盘对局，精彩地展示了兵中心对整个战场的影响。

text: Queen's Gambit
zh: 后翼弃兵

text: White: E.Geller
zh: 白方：E. 盖勒

text: Black: V.Simagin
zh: 黑方：V. 西马金

text: (19th USSR Championship 1951)
zh: （第十九届苏联锦标赛，1951年）

text: **1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6** (see next diagram)
zh:
**1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6**

（见下一图）

text: A classical position of pawn equilibrium in the centre.
zh: 这是中心兵保持均衡的典型局面。

text: There is a great choice of moves here for White. 4. Bg5 would continue the orthodox line in this variation.
zh: 白方在这里有很多选择。4. Bg5会进入这一变例的正统路线。

text: Either this, or 5. e3 - otherwise the pawn equilibrium will be upset to Black's advantage, for example 5. Bg5 cxd4 6. Nxd4 e5! **5... Nxd5 6. e3**
zh:
白方必须这样走，或者走5. e3，否则中心兵的均衡就会被打破，黑方得利。例如5. Bg5 cxd4 6. Nxd4 e5!。

**5... Nxd5 6. e3**

text: White could form a pawn centre at once by playing 6. e4. However, after 6... Nxc3 7. bxc3 cxd4 8. cxd4 Bb4+ 9. Bd2 Bxd2+ or 9... Qa5 followed by Bxd2+, occur numerous exchanges and this is not to everyone's taste. Nevertheless the presence of a pawn centre for White sets Black certain difficulties.
zh: 白方也可以立即走6. e4，建立兵中心。但6... Nxc3 7. bxc3 cxd4 8. cxd4 Bb4+ 9. Bd2之后，黑方可走9... Bxd2+，或9... Qa5再...Bxd2+，局面会发生大量兑换，并非所有棋手都喜欢这样。不过，白方的兵中心仍会给黑方造成一定困难。

text: In the 18th game of the return match for the world championship title between Alekhine and Euwe, followed 9... Bxd2+ 10. Qxd2 O-O 11. Bc4 Nc6 12. O-O b6 13. Rfd1 Bb7 14. Qf4 Rc8 15. d5! exd5 16. Bxd5 Qe7, when, by continuing 17. Qf5 with the threat Ng5, White could have obtained promising attacking chances. However, Alekhine played 17. Ng5 and Euwe defended himself cleverly by 17... Ne5 18. Bxb7 Ng6!
zh: 阿廖欣对尤伟的世界冠军回敬赛第18局，接着走9... Bxd2+ 10. Qxd2 O-O 11. Bc4 Nc6 12. O-O b6 13. Rfd1 Bb7 14. Qf4 Rc8 15. d5! exd5 16. Bxd5 Qe7。此时17. Qf5，威胁Ng5，可使白方获得很有希望的进攻机会。但阿廖欣走了17. Ng5，尤伟则以17... Ne5 18. Bxb7 Ng6!巧妙防守。

text: With the move 6. e3, White does not refrain from the plan of building up a pawn centre, but wants to realise this in more favourable conditions.
zh: 白方走6. e3并不是放弃建立兵中心的计划，而是希望在更有利的条件下实现它。

text: An interesting moment. If we look at this exchange as a separate tactical operation, then it should be condemned. It also gave rise to criticism by commentators of the game on the grounds that Black, firstly, strengthens White's pawn group in the centre and makes it easier for him to form a pawn centre, and, secondly, opens the b-file and thereby increases the active possibilities of the White pieces on the queen's flank.
zh: 这是一个有意思的时刻。如果只把这次兑换看成孤立的战术行动，它确实值得批评。评注者也正是据此提出异议：第一，黑方加强了白方的中心兵群，使白方更容易建立兵中心；第二，黑方打开b线，增加了白方子力在后翼积极活动的可能。

text: But nevertheless these considerations do not give grounds to criticise the exchange made by Black, which in fact is a very important link in his contemplated plan. Relying on the pawn tension "d4-c5" (pawn tension - is an arrangement of pawns whereby they attack each other), Black intended to concentrate the action of his heavy pieces on the c-file, and then, by taking on d4 at a suitable moment, to begin active play on this file. lt is unfavourable for White to eliminate the tension himself by dxc5, since after this the c4 point and the c3 pawn turn out to be potential weaknesses for him, subject to attack by the opponent. Consequently, when evaluating a move, it is necessary above all to establish whether or not it is a link in the plan and only then to look at its indefinite tactical significance for the given position.
zh: 然而，这些理由还不足以否定黑方的兑换，因为它实际上是黑方整体计划中极为重要的一环。黑方准备保持d4与c5两兵之间的紧张——所谓兵的紧张，就是双方的兵互相攻击——把重子集中到c线，再在适当时机于d4交换，沿该线展开积极行动。白方若主动以dxc5解除紧张，反而不利，因为c4格和c3兵会成为可能遭受攻击的弱点。因此，评价一步棋时，首先应弄清它是否属于某个计划，再考虑它在眼前局面中孤立的战术意义。

text: White claims his right to the centre, but the advance 11. d5, for the present, is not dangerous for Black. On this follows 11... e5, and the action of White's king's bishop will be limited by its own pawn chain. True, White obtains a well consolidated passed pawn in the centre, but Black's pieces (particularly the knight) can blockade it effectively from the d6 square, at the same time exerting strong pressure on the opponent's position. However, White is not obliged to play d5. He has formed a pawn centre and under its cover could strive to create more active play on one of the flanks. To counterbalance this, Black must try to organise an attack on the c-file.
zh: 白方确立了对中心的控制，但目前11. d5对黑方还不危险。黑方可用11... e5回应，使白方的王翼象受自身兵链限制。诚然，白方会得到一只受到牢固保护的中心通路兵，但黑方子力，尤其是马，可以在d6有效封锁它，同时向白方阵地施加强大压力。不过，白方并不一定要走d5。他已经建立兵中心，可以在其掩护下争取在某一翼展开积极行动。黑方则应以c线上的进攻相抗衡。

text: This move enters into Black's plan, but is made at the wrong time. He should first play 10... Qc7, so as not to allow the development of the bishop on f4. At the same time the queen move would assist in the carrying out of the main task - to concentrate fire on the c-file.
zh: 这步棋符合黑方的计划，但次序不对。黑方应先走10... Qc7，不让白象出到f4。这步动后同时也有助于完成主要任务：把火力集中到c线上。

text: Now Black has nowhere to place his queen and he experiences difficulties in connection with this.
zh: 现在，黑后找不到合适的位置，黑方因此陷入困难。

text: A good idea - transferring the black-squared bishop to the long diagonal to increase his piece influence in the centre and, in particular, to attack the d4 pawn.
zh: 构想不错：把黑格象转到长斜线，增强子力对中心的影响，尤其是攻击d4兵。

text: Now the exchange 7... Nxc3 can be positively censured, since Black gives up the pawn tension without carrying out appropriate preparations to seize the c-file. Soon it becomes clear that not Black, but White, will occupy the opened file and, possessing the pawn centre, will easily achieve a positional advantage.
zh: 现在可以明确批评7... Nxc3了，因为黑方还没做好夺取c线的准备，就主动解除了兵的紧张。很快就会看出，占据开放线的将是白方而非黑方；白方又拥有兵中心，很容易取得局面优势。

text: The consistent continuation was 13... Bf6, not fearing 14. dxc5 in view of 14... Nxc5 15. e5 Qc7. True, White could reply 14. Bd6 and Black would have to return with the bishop to e7, but this was sufficient to neutralise White's swoop. **14. cxd4 Bf6 15. Rac1**
zh:
贯彻原计划的下法是13... Bf6，不必害怕14. dxc5，因为14... Nxc5 15. e5 Qc7。白方固然可以14. Bd6，迫使黑象退回e7，但这样已足以化解白方的突袭。

**14. cxd4 Bf6 15. Rac1**

text: The invasion of the rook on c7 threatens a great deal of trouble and in the meantime Black can only postpone, but not prevent it.
zh: 白车侵入c7将制造巨大麻烦，而黑方只能暂缓，无法阻止。

text: On 17... Ra8, Black would likewise concede the open file under even worse conditions. White would play not an immediate 18. Rc7, because of 18... e5, but at first 18. Bd6. Simply 18. Rc2 was also good, doubling on the c-file.
zh: 若17... Ra8，黑方仍会让出开放线，而且条件更差。白方不会立即18. Rc7，以免黑方18... e5，而会先走18. Bd6。简单地18. Rc2、准备在c线叠车，也很好。

text: White has got everything he wants: occupation of the open line and invasion on it into the opponent's camp; invasion with the bishop on to the sixth rank; capture of the centre and harmonious action of his pieces. All these woes have befallen Black as a result of the serious planning error on the 13th move.
zh: 白方想要的一切都实现了：占据开放线并沿线侵入敌阵，象侵入第六横线，控制中心，子力协调配合。黑方遭受这一切，根源都在于第13步那个严重的计划错误。

text: Of course, this sortie with a lone queen cannot help matters.
zh: 后孤军出击，当然无力挽救局面。

text: He could not play 22. Rxd7 because of 22... Qb1+, but now Black will be constantly threatened with this combination.
zh: 立即22. Rxd7不行，因为22... Qb1+；现在，这个组合将始终威胁着黑方。

text: White's pieces create havoc on the seventh rank. Black puts up further resistance through inertia.
zh: 白方子力在第七横线横冲直撞，黑方只是在惯性地继续抵抗。

text: **25... Qb1 26. Qe7 Rc8 27. Rxh7 Nxh7 28. Qxe6+ Kg7 29. Qd7+ Kg8 30. Qxc8+ Kg7 31. Qc7+ Kg8 32. e6 1-0** We look at one more example, which is not only extremely instructive but also brilliant in content and form, and which illustrates a breakthrough with the central pawn phalanx, brought about by the creative inspiration of Alekhine.
zh:
**25... Qb1 26. Qe7 Rc8 27. Rxh7 Nxh7 28. Qxe6+ Kg7 29. Qd7+ Kg8 30. Qxc8+ Kg7 31. Qc7+ Kg8 32. e6 1-0**

再看一个不仅极富启发性，而且内容与表现都十分精彩的例子。阿廖欣以富有创造力的构想，展示了中心兵阵如何实施突破。

text: Blumenfeld Gambit
zh: 布卢门费尔德弃兵

text: White: S.Tarrasch
zh: 白方：S. 塔拉什

text: Black: A.Alekhine
zh: 黑方：A. 阿廖欣

text: (Pistyan 1922)
zh: （皮斯蒂安，1922年）

text: The idea, lying at the basis of this sudden pawn sacrifice, is to pursue the aim of creating a well-fortified mobile pawn centre. Here, the positional advantage (pawn centre), as it were, offsets the material advantage (extra pawn).
zh: 这次突然弃兵的基本构想，是建立一个稳固而能够前冲的兵中心。可以说，黑方用局面优势——兵中心——补偿对手的子力优势——多出的一兵。

text: Admittedly, practice has shown that, instead of accepting the sacrifice, it is better for White to continue 5. Bg5. By pinning the knight, he strengthens the d5 pawn, which cramps Black, and threatens to form a pawn phalanx in the centre himself, after e4.
zh: 不过，实践表明，白方最好不接受弃兵，而走5. Bg5。牵制黑马可以巩固限制着黑方的d5兵，并准备自己冲起e4，在中心组成兵阵。

text: In the game Dus Chotimirsky-Levenfish (Moscow vs. Leningrad match 1922), Black tried to defend himself by 5... bxc4, but after 6. e4 Ba6 7. Nc3 Qa5 White could have given the opponent irresistible difficulties. For example, if 8... d6, then 9. dxe6 fxe6 10. Be2 Be7 11. O-O O-O 12. e5 dxe5 13. Nxe5 with an overwhelming initiative.
zh: 在杜斯-霍季米尔斯基对列文菲什一局中（莫斯科对列宁格勒对抗赛，1922年），黑方试图以5... bxc4防守。但6. e4 Ba6 7. Nc3 Qa5之后，白方本可给对手造成难以克服的困难。
editorial_note: 用户校对决定：删除中文中‘例如，’起的全部变化和相关缺漏校勘注；原书漏列白方第8步，且用户指出该变化并非白方最严厉的手段。英文原文保留备查。

text: Black also suffered a reverse in the game Grunfeld-Bogolyubov, (Vienna 1922), where, after 5... h6 6. Bxf6 Qxf6 7. Nc3 b4 8. Nb5 Na6 9. e4, he tried taking the b2 pawn with the queen and lost quickly. By continuing 9... e5, with the aim of locking the position (10. d6 Bb7), Black could put resistance but his position dn nevertheless remains cramped.
zh: 在格林菲尔德对波戈留波夫一局中（维也纳，1922年），黑方同样遭到失败。5... h6 6. Bxf6 Qxf6 7. Nc3 b4 8. Nb5 Na6 9. e4之后，黑方试图用后吃b2兵，很快就输了。若9... e5，力求封闭局面，10. d6 Bb7之后尚可抵抗，但黑方仍然局促。

text: **5. dxe6 fxe6 6. cxb5 d5 7. e3**
zh: **5. dxe6 fxe6 6. cxb5 d5 7. e3**

text: A very passive plan. White simply develops his pieces without thinking about countering the main link in Black's plan - the advance... e5. His task would undoubtedly be made difficult if White were to play now Bf4 or Bg5. It is unfavourable for Black to win back the pawn 7... Qa5+ 8. Qd2 Qxb5 in view of 9. e4. In the event of 7. Bg5 Nbd7, possible is 8. Nbd2 and if 8... e5?, then 9. e4. **7... Bd6**
zh:
计划过于消极。白方只是单纯出子，没有考虑阻止黑方计划的关键环节——冲起e5。此时Bf4或Bg5，无疑会增加黑方实现计划的困难。黑方若7... Qa5+ 8. Qd2 Qxb5吃回一兵，会因9. e4而不利。7. Bg5 Nbd7之后，白方可走8. Nbd2；若8... e5?，则9. e4。

**7... Bd6**

text: Naturally! The pawn sacrifice has fully justified itself. Black now carries out the advance of the e-pawn without difficulty, while the bishops are placed on adjacent diagonals, where they will rake the centre and White's king's side castled position. After the march of the pawn... e5-e4, the knight f3 will have to look for another haven, after which the h2 and g2 points become real weaknesses. **8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8**
zh:
理所当然！黑方的弃兵已获得充分补偿。现在他可以顺利冲起e兵，双象则分别占据相邻斜线，瞄准中心和白方短易位后的王城。一旦...e5-e4，f3马就必须另寻落脚点，h2和g2也会成为切实的弱点。

**8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8**

text: A full mobilisation of forces. The entire Black army has been marshalled behind the three-pawn central phalanx, ready for a ramming campaign against the opponent. All this has been achieved at the cost of a single pawn.
zh: 黑方完成了全面动员。全部子力在由三兵组成的中心兵阵后集结，准备向对手发起猛烈冲击，而这一切的代价仅仅是一兵。

text: However formidable the storm hanging over White's position may be, he intends to meet it fully armed. Tarrasch organises a well-composed plan of defence of the king's “fortress".
zh: 尽管白方阵地上空风暴将至，塔拉什仍打算严阵以待。他为王城组织了一套周密的防守计划。

text: The offensive begins. The threat is... e4 with a subsequent attack on the h2 point. In order to defend it, he needs to transfer the knight, via d2, to f1. First he must move the rook away - but where? Only to e1, since the d1 square, though on an open file, must be occupied by the knight, in order to defend the f2 square which is dangerously weakened after the removal of the king's rook. And so White's immediate defensive operation consists of the moves Rfe1, Nd1 and the manoeuvre Nd2-f1.
zh: 攻势开始了。黑方威胁...e4，再进攻h2。为了保护h2，白方须将马经d2调到f1。但首先要挪开车——挪到哪里？只能是e1。d1虽然位于开放线上，却必须留给另一只马，用来保护王翼车离开后变得十分薄弱的f2格。因此，白方眼前的防守部署是Rfe1、Nd1，再以Nd2-f1调马。

text: Nevertheless there remains a vulnerable point in White's defence - the g2 square. In the end it is precisely here where Black aims his blow, but the effectiveness of this blow will, all the same, be based on the breakthrough of the pawn centre.
zh: 不过，白方防线仍留下一个薄弱环节：g2格。黑方最终正是瞄准这里发动打击，但这一打击能够奏效，根本上仍依赖中心兵的突破。

text: Black threatens a direct attack on the f2 and h2 points after each of the Black knights goes to g4.
zh: 两只黑马无论哪一只进入g4，都将直接威胁f2和h2。

text: **16. Nd1 Nfg4 17. Bxg4 Nxg4 18. Nf1 Qg5**
zh: **16. Nd1 Nfg4 17. Bxg4 Nxg4 18. Nf1 Qg5**

text: White has succeeded in firmly defending the f2 and h2 points, but Black begins to prepare an attack on the g2 square. Included in his plan is the knight manoeuvre... Nh6-f5-h4. Other threats are also growing, such as... Rf3! In short it is difficult to put up with the knight on g4; he has to make a move which weakens his position.
zh: 白方虽然已牢牢守住f2和h2，黑方却开始准备进攻g2，其计划包括...Nh6-f5-h4的调马路线。...Rf3!等其他威胁也在酝酿。总之，白方难以容忍黑马停在g4，只能以削弱自身局面的冲兵将它赶走。

text: Also securing the defence of the g2 point (21... Nh4 22. Rg1). **21... d4!**

But now comes the advance in the centre, after which the White defence caves in. The basis of this advance is the weakening of the g3 point. On 22. exd4 follows 22... e3 and a decisive invasion of the Black pieces on g3 cannot be averted.
zh: 但现在，黑方在中心发动冲击，白方防线随之崩溃。这次冲击的依据是g3格已经削弱。若22. exd4，则22... e3，黑方子力决定性地侵入g3已无法阻止。

text: There is already no satisfactory defence. In this way, White at least averts the double attack of the queen from the e5 square, which is threatened in several variations. For example, if 24. Bd2, then 24... Ng3+ 25. Kg1 (25. fxg3 Qxg3 26. Ng4 Qxe1+ and mate on the following move) 25... Ne2+ 26. Kh1 Qe5. **24... Ng3+ 25. Kg1 Bd5**
zh:
白方已经没有令人满意的防守。这步动象至少避开了若干变化中黑后到e5形成的双重攻击。例如24. Bd2 Ng3+ 25. Kg1（25. fxg3 Qxg3 26. Ng4 Qxe1+，下一步将杀）25... Ne2+ 26. Kh1 Qe5。

**24... Ng3+ 25. Kg1 Bd5**

text: Black is not content with the win of the exchange after 25... d2.
zh: 黑方不满足于25... d2之后仅仅得半子。

text: This is where a mobile part of a pawn centre sometimes breaks through! Now Black wins the exchange, creating a mating attack.
zh: 能向前冲击的中心兵，竟然可以突破到如此深入的位置！现在黑方既能得半子，又能组织杀王攻势。

text: **32. Rf1 Nxf1 33. Nxf1 Be6 34. Kh1 Bxh3**
zh: **32. Rf1 Nxf1 33. Nxf1 Be6 34. Kh1 Bxh3**

text: All this is a consequence of the powerful role which the pawn centre plays. Also now the e and d pawns disorganise the whole of White’s defence.
zh: 这一切都是强大兵中心发挥作用的结果。此时，e兵和d兵仍在瓦解白方的整条防线。

text: Allowing himself the possibility of losing “beautifully”.
zh: 白方给自己留下了“漂亮”地输棋的机会。

text: Black's pawn on d2 serves as a tacit reproach for White's decision to accept the opening sacrifice.
zh: 黑方d2兵仿佛在无声地责问白方：开局时为什么要接受弃兵？

text: In several contemporary opening systems, for example in the King’s Indian Defence, attempts are made to prove that the construction of a pawn centre, if it is pinned down, is not so dangerous and that danger is only threatened by the side having the mobile pawn centre. Adherents to this view obviously reckon that it is always possible to counter the static pawn centre with flank operations, while the centre itself is troubled from the side. However, the fact of the matter is that in flank battles the chances, for the most part, arise for the player who controls the centre.
zh: 在一些现代开局体系中，例如古印度防御，人们试图证明：只要能够限制兵中心的活动，允许对方建立兵中心也没有那么危险；真正有威胁的只是能够向前冲击的兵中心。持这种观点的人显然认为，对固定的兵中心，总可以用侧翼行动来抗衡，并从侧面加以冲击。但问题在于，两翼战斗中的机会，通常仍属于控制中心的一方。

text: The danger of disregarding an immobile centre are well illustrated by the following game:
zh: 下面的对局清楚说明：即使兵中心暂时不能移动，轻视它仍然十分危险。

text:
King’s Indian Defence

White: S. Zhukhovitsky
zh:
古印度防御

白方：S. 茹霍维茨基

text: Black: M.Taimanov
zh: 黑方：M. 泰曼诺夫

text: 1/2-final 25th USSR Championship
zh: （第二十五届苏联锦标赛半决赛）

text:
As distinct from the Grünfeld Defence (3... d5), where, to a certain extent, the White pawn centre turns out to be an object of attack, in the present variation of the King’s Indian Defence it is strong and solid but, in return, not dynamic.

**4. e4 O-O 5. f3 c6 6. Bg5**
zh:
格林菲尔德防御（3... d5）在一定程度上把白方兵中心作为攻击目标；而在本局的古印度防御变例中，白方兵中心强大而稳固，代价则是缺乏机动性。

**4. e4 O-O 5. f3 c6 6. Bg5**

text: White has a three-pawn phalanx in the centre, and it is not possible to loosen this menacing wall with a counter-advance of central pawns. Consequently, he is guaranteed a supremacy in the centre for quite some time to come.
zh: 白方在中心形成三兵阵，黑方无法用中心兵的反冲击动摇这道强大的屏障。因此，在此后相当长的时间内，白方都能保持中心优势。

text: Some compensation for Black is provided by his very good development of pieces on the king's flank. His plan will consist of removing if only the c4 pawn from White's pawn group in the centre. However the e4 and d4 pawns remain in their dominating positions and this allows White to soon launch an attack on the king's flank.
zh: 黑方王翼出子良好，获得了一定补偿。他准备至少先消除白方中心兵群中的c4兵。然而e4、d4两兵仍占据主导位置，使白方能够迅速发动王翼进攻。

text: With the aim of playing... b5. This artificial and not very effective plan was also tried in the third Botvinnik-Smyslov match - but Smyslov had no success with it. This also is clear - such a plan runs counter to the classical principle of a quick and purposeful development of pieces.
zh: 准备...b5。这种生硬而效果有限的计划，也曾在鲍特维尼克与斯梅斯洛夫的第三次对抗赛中出现，但斯梅斯洛夫未能借此成功。原因不难理解：它违背了迅速、有目的地出子这一经典原则。

text: Black should proceed along proven ways and try to prepare the move... e5 by... d6,... Qc7 and ... Nbd7.
zh: 黑方应采用经受过实践检验的方法，以...d6、...Qc7和...Nbd7准备冲起e5。

text: The already known to us attacking march of the rook's pawn, which, thanks to the advance of the g6 pawn, guarantees the opening of the end file.
zh: 这是我们已经熟悉的边兵进攻。由于黑方g兵已冲起g6，白方可以确保打开h线。

text: Also a type of exchange, evoked by the weakening of the approach to the Black king's position. But nevertheless the natural 9. Bxc4 (or 9. e5 and then Nxc4) should be preferred to this sacrifice of a pawn.
zh: 这也是利用黑王外围防线削弱而进行的典型兑换。不过，与这种弃兵下法相比，顺理成章的9. Bxc4，或9. e5后再Nxc4，更值得选择。

text: An interesting development of the attack, linked to beautiful mating variations. Thus, if now 10... Nxh5, then 11. Rxh5 gxh5 12. Qg5, and mate is already unavoidable. Likewise after 10... gxh5 11. Qg5 Ne8 12. Qxh5 f6 13. Bxg7 or 13. Be3, White's attack must be crowned with decisive success. **10... Be6 11. e5** Also not bad was 11. Bxg7 Kxg7 12. hxg6 fxg6 13. Qh6+ with e5 to follow. **11... Ne8 12. Bxg7 Nxg7 13. hxg6 hxg6**
zh:
白方以一种有趣的方式继续进攻，其中包含漂亮的杀王变化。若10... Nxh5，则11. Rxh5 gxh5 12. Qg5，黑方已无法避免被杀。若10... gxh5，则11. Qg5 Ne8 12. Qxh5 f6 13. Bxg7或13. Be3，白方的攻势同样应能决定胜负。

**10... Be6 11. e5**

11. Bxg7 Kxg7 12. hxg6 fxg6 13. Qh6+，随后e5，也不错。

**11... Ne8 12. Bxg7 Nxg7 13. hxg6 hxg6**

text: Black had more promise of defensive resources with 13... h5.
zh: 13... h5能为黑方保留更多防守资源。

text: On 14... Nh5 would clearly follow 15. g4, but now White recovers the sacrificed pawn whilst maintaining the attack.
zh: 若14... Nh5，白方显然走15. g4。实战中，白方既能吃回弃掉的一兵，又能保持攻势。

text: **15. Qh7+ Kf7 16. Rh6 Rg8** 16... Bf5 is no good in view of 17. g4, but after the text move Black loses not one but two pawns. However, there was no choice. Admittedly, by playing 16... Qe8, he could retain material equilibrium, but he falls under an irresistible attack: 17. Be2! (threat: 18. Qxg6+ Kg8 19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. f4 and wins) 17... g5 (or 17... Bf5 18. e6+! Kxe6 19. g4! Bd3 20. Qxg7 Rf7 21. Rh8; it is interesting that in this variation it is not possible to take the knight at once by 19. Qxg7, in view of 19... Rg8 20. Qh7 g5) 18. f4 g4 19. Bxg4 Bxg4 20. Qg6+ Kg8 21. Qxg4 f5 22. Qh4 and the threat e6 is decisive, since on... e6 follows mate in two moves. **17. exf6 exf6 18. Qxg6+ Kf8 19. Qxf6+**
zh:
**15. Qh7+ Kf7 16. Rh6 Rg8**

16... Bf5因17. g4而不行，但实战这步棋使黑方要丢的不是一兵，而是两兵。不过，他已经别无选择。16... Qe8固然可维持子力平衡，却会遭到难以抵挡的进攻：17. Be2!，威胁18. Qxg6+ Kg8 19. Qh7+ Kf7 20. f4获胜；17... g5（或17... Bf5 18. e6+! Kxe6 19. g4! Bd3 20. Qxg7 Rf7 21. Rh8。有意思的是，在这一变化中不能立即19. Qxg7吃马，因为19... Rg8 20. Qh7 g5）18. f4 g4 19. Bxg4 Bxg4 20. Qg6+ Kg8 21. Qxg4 f5 22. Qh4，e6的威胁决定胜负，因为...e6会遭到两步杀。

**17. exf6 exf6 18. Qxg6+ Kf8 19. Qxf6+**

text: A sensible decision. Playing for the attack at all costs was risky. On 19. O-O-O, Black would obtain counterattacking chances by 19... Nd7 with the threat of... Bf5 or... Nf5.
zh: 明智的决定。不惜一切代价坚持进攻反而有风险。若19. O-O-O，黑方可走19... Nd7，威胁...Bf5或...Nf5，取得反击机会。

text: White has won a pawn: besides this, a phalanx consisting of two connected passed pawns has been created for him on the king's flank. In the endgame, such a superiority is realised quite easily, but this is still a long way off. There is a rather sharp middlegame in prospect, in which neither king can feel secure. This gives Black definite counter-chances, he needs only to complicate the game and avoid exchanges which draw the game closer to an ending.
zh: 白方多出一兵，还在王翼形成两个相连的通路兵。在残局中，这种优势较容易兑现，但眼下离残局还远。接下来仍是一场尖锐的中局战斗，双方的王都不安全。这给了黑方一定反击机会：他只需使局面复杂化，避免将对局推向残局的兑换。

text: However, why was it that White's strong attack, into which went so much ingenuity, bore such modest fruit? This happened because White, relying on his pawn centre, hurled himself too impetuously into an attack on the flank, leaving his king in the centre. This was reckless and premature. That is why White's 9th move should be censured.
zh: 然而，白方如此富于巧思的猛烈进攻，为什么收获却这样有限？原因在于，他过分依赖兵中心，急于向侧翼发起进攻，却把自己的王留在中心。这种做法冒进而且为时过早，因此白方第9步值得批评。

text: If after **21... Nf5 22. Rh7+ Kd6 23. Nge2 Nd7** (Black mobilises his reserves, exploiting the fact that White cannot castle in view of 24... Ne3 winning the g2 pawn) **24. Kf2** Black had not made the mistake **24... c5?** then he not only could have defended himself successfully, but also had available interesting possibilities of counterattack.
zh: 实战**21... Nf5 22. Rh7+ Kd6 23. Nge2 Nd7** **24. Kf2**之后，黑方若不犯**24... c5?**的错误，不仅能够成功防守，还拥有值得注意的反击机会。其中23... Nd7调动了后备力量，并利用了白方无法易位这一点：白方一旦易位，黑方就能24... Ne3吃掉g2兵。

text: He should play 24... Nf6 25. Rh1 Raf8! forestalling the unpleasant move g4 and securing the position of the knight on f5, which exerts strong pressure on the centre and the king's flank. On 26. g4? (after 25... Raf8) follows 26... Nxg4+! 27. fxg4 Nxd4+, and White has to give up the rook a1, since not possible is either 28. Kg3 Rxg4+ 29. Kh2 Nf3+ mating, or 28. Kg1 Rxg4+ 29. Bg2 Nf3+ 30. Kf1 Nh4+. If, instead of 26. g4, White continues with the more modest 26. g3 (you see, it is necessary to bring the bishop into play!), then Black obtains a threatening attack by 26... Ne4+ (27. fxe4 Nxg3+ 28. Kg2 Nxh1+ 29. Kxh1 Rg7! and wins).
zh: 黑方应走24... Nf6 25. Rh1 Raf8!，防住讨厌的g4，并巩固f5马的位置。这只马向中心和王翼施加强大压力。若26. g4?，则26... Nxg4+! 27. fxg4 Nxd4+，白方必须放弃a1车，因为28. Kg3 Rxg4+ 29. Kh2 Nf3+将杀，而28. Kg1 Rxg4+ 29. Bg2 Nf3+ 30. Kf1 Nh4+也不行。若白方改走较谨慎的26. g3——毕竟必须把象出出来——黑方则以26... Ne4+取得强大攻势：27. fxe4 Nxg3+ 28. Kg2 Nxh1+ 29. Kxh1 Rg7!，黑方获胜。

text: After the "active" **24... c5** came a quick catastrophe, and there is no need to explain in detail the finale of the game:
zh: 实战中看似“积极”的**24... c5**，却使黑方迅速崩溃。此后的收尾已无需详细解释：

text: White rids himself of the weak d4 pawn and introduces all the inactive pieces into battle; all this is a result of Black's light-headed "attack" on the centre.
zh: 白方摆脱了d4弱兵，并把所有原先闲置的棋子投入战斗。这都是黑方轻率地“进攻”中心所造成的结果。

text: **26... Rab8 27. Rb1 d4 28. Nxe6! dxc3 29. Nxc5 Rxb2+**
zh: **26... Rab8 27. Rb1 d4 28. Nxe6! dxc3 29. Nxc5 Rxb2+**

text: The piece, but not the game, can be saved by the move 29... Kxc5, on which would follow 30. Rc7+ Kd6 31. Rxc4 Rxb2+ 32. Rxb2 cxb2 33. Rb4 with an easy win in the endgame. **30. Rxb2 cxb2 31. Ne4+ Ke5 32. Rb7 c3 33. Nxc3 Rc8 34. Na4 Rc2+ 35. Be2 b1=Q 36. Rxb1 Rxa2 37. Nc3 Rc2 38. Rb3 a5 39. Ra3 a4 40. Nxa4 Nd4 41. Re3+**
zh:
29... Kxc5可以避免失子，却无法挽救败局：30. Rc7+ Kd6 31. Rxc4 Rxb2+ 32. Rxb2 cxb2 33. Rb4，白方轻松赢下残局。

**30. Rxb2 cxb2 31. Ne4+ Ke5 32. Rb7 c3 33. Nxc3 Rc8 34. Na4 Rc2+ 35. Be2 b1=Q 36. Rxb1 Rxa2 37. Nc3 Rc2 38. Rb3 a5 39. Ra3 a4 40. Nxa4 Nd4 41. Re3+**

text: The time control passed, White will not “miss" anything; therefore 1-0
zh: 时限已过，白方不会再有“漏着”，黑方遂认输。

text: We refer to the pawn phalanx. This name is given to some (most frequently two) connected pawns, out of which at least one is situated on an open file. The phalanx - this is clearly dynamic, connected with forward movement. This sort of pawn-pair potentially has dynamic power, capable of breaking through the enemy front. The central phalanx with pawns on the d and c-files is a very active weapon. Often another phalanx is met in practice, made up of the e and f-pawns; we give it detailed consideration in the next chapter. Here, however, we stay with the basic aspect of the phalanx, consisting of the “hanging” pawns, i.e. pawns which are situated on two open files and isolated from the rest of the pawn chain. Usually the "hanging" phalanx comes about on the c and d-files, since its formation for the most part is connected with definite opening systems and variations. We look at a few examples.
zh: 下面讨论兵阵。这个名称指若干个相连的兵，最常见的是两个，其中至少一兵位于开放线上。兵阵这一概念强调的是向前冲击的动态力量：这样一对兵具有突破敌方防线的潜力。由c兵和d兵组成的中心兵阵是一件十分积极的武器。实战中还经常出现由e兵和f兵组成的兵阵，下一章将详细讨论。这里先考察兵阵的一种主要形态——“悬兵”，即位于两条开放线上、与其余兵链隔离的两个兵。悬兵通常出现在c线和d线上，因为其形成大多与特定开局体系及变例有关。下面看几个例子。

text: In the 3rd game of the match Levenfish-Botvinnik, 1937, after: **1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qc2 d5 5. cxd5 Qxd5 6. e3 c5 7. a3 Bxc3+ 8. bxc3 b6 9. Nf3 Nbd7 10. c4 Qd6 11. Bb2 Bb7 12. Be2 cxd4 13. exd4** the following position was reached:
zh:
1937年列文菲什对鲍特维尼克对抗赛第3局，经过以下招法，形成图示局面：

**1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. Qc2 d5 5. cxd5 Qxd5 6. e3 c5 7. a3 Bxc3+ 8. bxc3 b6 9. Nf3 Nbd7 10. c4 Qd6 11. Bb2 Bb7 12. Be2 cxd4 13. exd4**

text: White has obtained “hanging' pawns on the d4 and c4 squares. This pawn-group is isolated from the rest of the White pawns; at the same time it is situated on open files and therefore, if it is slowed down, will become an object of attack for the opponent's heavy pieces. Both these factors characterise the weak side of a “hanging centre". But it also has a great quality - mobility. The “hanging centre" is above all a phalanx - and if it gets a chance to display its dynamic virtue and advances, then it might sweep away everything in its path.
zh: 白方在d4和c4形成悬兵。这组兵与其他白兵隔离，又位于开放线上，一旦被限制活动，就会成为对方重子的攻击目标。这两个因素体现了“悬兵中心”的弱点。但它还有一项重要长处：机动性。悬兵中心首先是一支兵阵；一旦有机会发挥其动态力量向前冲击，就可能扫清前进道路上的一切障碍。

text: Let us look at the further development of the struggle:
zh: 再看实战如何发展：

text: **13... O-O 14. O-O Ng4 15. h3 Bxf3 16. hxg4 Bxe2 17. Qxe2 Rac8**
zh: **13... O-O 14. O-O Ng4 15. h3 Bxf3 16. hxg4 Bxe2 17. Qxe2 Rac8**

text: The c4 pawn is the vulnerable point in White's “"hanging centre" and it is here that Black directs his blows.
zh: c4兵是白方悬兵中心的薄弱环节，黑方正是把攻击矛头指向这里。

text: White prepares a bold advance of the central pawns, in reply to which Black continues to concentrate pressure on the c-file. If he wants to, Black could prevent the opponent's plan by 18... Re8, and if 19. Qf1, then 19... Qf4, but, not without foundation, he considers that the advance d5 is a double-edged weapon. The pawn has nowhere to go, further than the d5 square, while then Black takes control of the c5 square and pins down the c4 pawn. And the pawn, deprived of mobility and backward, is a serious positional weakness.
zh: 白方准备大胆地向前冲起中心兵，黑方则继续向c线集中压力。黑方如果愿意，本可18... Re8，19. Qf1 Qf4，阻止对手的计划。不过，他认为d5是一把双刃剑，这也并非没有根据：d兵到达d5后便难以继续前进，黑方则能控制c5，使c4兵动弹不得。一只失去机动性而又落后的兵，是严重的局面弱点。

text: Black prevents ... g5. If 21... Re8, then 22. Ba3 Nc5, and White can play with advantage 23. g5. **22. a5 bxa5 23. Ba3 Nc5 24. Reb1 a6 25. Qe1 Rfc8 26. Qxa5 Qd7 27. Rb6**
zh:
黑方防止白方冲起g5。若21... Re8，则22. Ba3 Nc5 23. g5，白方有利。

**22. a5 bxa5 23. Ba3 Nc5 24. Reb1 a6 25. Qe1 Rfc8 26. Qxa5 Qd7 27. Rb6**

text: With the aim of effecting a further advance of the d-pawn, which would follow at once after 27... Qxg4. **27... Nd3?**
zh:
准备继续冲起d兵。若27... Qxg4，白方便立即这样做。

**27... Nd3?**

text: Leading to defeat. After 27... Ne4, as shown by numerous analyses of the present position, Black should not lose.
zh: 败招。对这一局面的大量分析表明，黑方若27... Ne4，应当不会输。

text: Because of the threat Qd5+ Black loses the exchange.
zh: 由于Qd5+的威胁，黑方将丢掉半子。

text: **28... Nf4 29. dxc7** and White won

Also in the next example (Sokolsky-Botvinnik, Semi-final 11th USSR Championship 1938), White does not succeed in making the opponent's “hanging” centre an object of attack; on the contrary, its dynamic power tells quite quickly.
zh: 下例是索科尔斯基对鲍特维尼克一局（第十一届苏联锦标赛半决赛，1938年）。白方同样没能把对手的悬兵中心变为攻击目标；相反，悬兵的动态力量很快便显现出来。

text: With the threat of... d4.
While now... Nxe3 is threatened.
zh: 现在又威胁...Nxe3。

text: **19. Qd3 Nde5 20. Nxe5 Qxe5 21. Ng3 Qf6 22. Nh1 d4 23. Qe2 Ne5 24. exd4 cxd4 25. Rxc8 Bxc8**
zh: **19. Qd3 Nde5 20. Nxe5 Qxe5 21. Ng3 Qf6 22. Nh1 d4 23. Qe2 Ne5 24. exd4 cxd4 25. Rxc8 Bxc8**

text: This is better than 25... Rxc8. The rook needs to stay on the d-file in order to support the advance of the passed pawn. At the same time,... Bg4 is threatened.
zh: 这比25... Rxc8好。车须留在d线上，支持通路兵冲起，同时还制造了...Bg4的威胁。

text: The “hanging” pawn breaks through.
zh: 悬兵突破了！

text: 29... Qxe5 was also possible.
zh: 29... Qxe5也可以。

text: **30. Re8+ Rxe8 31. Qxf6 Be2 32. Ng3 Bg7 33. Qc6 Bb5** and Black soon won.
zh:
**30. Re8+ Rxe8 31. Qxf6 Be2 32. Ng3 Bg7 33. Qc6 Bb5**

黑方很快获胜。

text: The march of the d-pawn - one of the main components of the "hanging" pawn centre - proved decisive.
zh: 作为悬兵中心主要成员之一的d兵，其向前冲击决定了胜负。

text: We have already spoken about the role of the pawn centre, which in individual positions might prove to be not a strength but a weakness, not a weapon, but an object of attack.
zh: 我们已经谈到，在某些具体局面中，兵中心并非强点而是弱点，并非进攻武器而是攻击目标。

text: The weakness of a central pawn is a serious positional minus, particularly when it is subjected to an attack on the open files and ranks. We will look at a few examples which allow us to understand how positional processes attend the weakening of the central pawns.
zh: 中心兵薄弱是严重的局面劣势，尤其是它能沿开放的纵线和横线受到攻击时。下面的几个例子，将帮助我们理解中心兵变弱时，局面会如何随之演变。

text: Here we have a position from the 19th game of the Tarrasch-Chigorin match of 1893.The White pawn on e4 is under attack. Black intends this planned objective, arising from the following considerations: the e4 pawn lacks pawn cover, it is also difficult to defend it with pieces, since White's king's bishop has been exchanged, while it is not so easy to mobilise his queen's rook; finally the central pawns are convenient targets for attack on the open lines - the e-file and the a8-h1 diagonal, which are in Black's hands. At one point, as far back as the opening itself, White played f4, without looking ahead to the future consequences of this advance.
zh: 图示局面出自1893年塔拉什对齐果林对抗赛第19局。白方e4兵正遭受攻击。黑方选择它作为计划的目标，基于以下考虑：e4兵没有其他兵保护；白方的王翼象已经兑掉，后翼车又难以及时调出，因此用棋子守兵也困难；此外，黑方掌握e线和a8-h1斜线，中心兵正是这些开放线路上便于攻击的目标。早在开局阶段，白方就走了f4，却没有预见到这步冲兵的长远后果。

text: Further events developed in the following way.
zh: 实战接着这样发展：

text: White already has to make this awkward move, locking in his own bishop, in order to defend the ill-fated pawn. On 18. Qd3 follows 18... Qe7 19. Nbd2 d5! 20. e5 Qxb4. 18.
