Qf3 is also bad: then, besides 18... Qe7, possible is an immediate 18... Nxe4 19. Nxe4 d5 or 19. Rxe4 Rxe4 20. Nxe4 Qe7 21. Nbd2 Re8 22. Nf6+ Bxf6 23. Qxb7 Qe3+. **18... Qd7 19. h3 Re7 20. Re2 Rae8 21. Qf1** 21. Qe1 does not save the pawn in view of 21... Qc6 22. c3 Nxe4 23. Nxe4 f5. **21... h5 22. h4 Qg4 23. Qf2 Qxh4** and White lost.
zh:
为了保护这只处境不妙的兵，白方已经不得不走出这步别扭的退马，堵住自己的象。若18. Qd3，则18... Qe7 19. Nbd2 d5! 20. e5 Qxb4。18. Qf3也不好，黑方除了18... Qe7，还可立即18... Nxe4：19. Nxe4 d5，或19. Rxe4 Rxe4 20. Nxe4 Qe7 21. Nbd2 Re8 22. Nf6+ Bxf6 23. Qxb7 Qe3+。

**18... Qd7 19. h3 Re7 20. Re2 Rae8 21. Qf1**

21. Qe1也保不住兵，因为21... Qc6 22. c3 Nxe4 23. Nxe4 f5。

**21... h5 22. h4 Qg4 23. Qf2 Qxh4**

白方败。

text: A similar scheme of attack on the central White pawns was carried out virtually in the opening in a game Ravinsky-Romanovsky (Leningrad 1926): Also here the source of the weakness of the e4 pawn, deprived of pawn cover, is the advance f4, made even on the 4th move after 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 e5 3. dxe5 Nxe5 4. f4.
zh: 在拉文斯基对罗曼诺夫斯基一局中（列宁格勒，1926年），类似的进攻白方中心兵的部署，几乎在开局就已实现。这里，e4兵失去兵的保护而成为弱点，同样源于f4。白方甚至在第4步就这样走了：1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 e5 3. dxe5 Nxe5 4. f4。

text: In the diagrammed position White has further trouble in that the rooks cannot be included in the defence of the e4 pawn. Admittedly he has the white-squared bishop available for this, which Tarrasch did not have, while Black's queen's bishop does not reinforce the attack on the centre from the b7 square; nevertheless this bishop finds another way to join in the attack on the e4 pawn.
zh: 图示局面中，白方还有一重困难：双车无法参加对e4兵的防守。诚然，他仍有白格象可用，这是塔拉什所没有的；黑方的后翼象也没有在b7加强对中心的压力。但这只象找到了另一条参加攻击e4兵的路线。

text: And so, Black already threatens to take the e4 pawn. Therefore:
zh: 黑方已经威胁吃掉e4兵，因此白方走：

text: This is the possibility we referred to. Black attacks the e4 pawn for a fourth time. The continuation 13. exf5 Qxe3 14. O-O-O Qxf3 15. Nxf3 Nd5 was not comforting for White, since it would dangerously weaken the e3 point, but nevertheless he should give it preference since the attempt to defend the pawn is demolished. **13. Ng3 Bxe4! 14. Ngxe4 Nxe4 15. Bxe4 d5**
zh:
这就是刚才提到的可能性。黑方第四次攻击e4兵。13. exf5 Qxe3 14. O-O-O Qxf3 15. Nxf3 Nd5并不能令白方满意，因为e3格会变得十分薄弱；尽管如此，他仍应选择这个变化，因为继续保兵的企图会被彻底粉碎。

**13. Ng3 Bxe4! 14. Ngxe4 Nxe4 15. Bxe4 d5**

text: White has avoided material loss, but the attack on his central pawn allows the opponent to develop a very strong attack on the king, which has not managed to castle.
zh: 白方虽然避免了子力损失，但黑方借助对中心兵的攻击，转而对尚未易位的白王发动了强大攻势。

text: **16. Bxd5 Qxe3+ 17. Qxe3 Rxe3+ 18. Kd1 Rd8 19. Bxc6 Red3!**
zh: **16. Bxd5 Qxe3+ 17. Qxe3 Rxe3+ 18. Kd1 Rd8 19. Bxc6 Red3!**

text: The Black rooks break through to the second rank, after which White cannot resist for very long.
zh: 黑方双车即将侵入第二横线，白方无法再抵抗多久。

text: One is drawn to the conclusion that a serious reason for a weakness of a central (or indeed any other) pawn is the impossibility of defending it with pawns from adjacent files. It goes without saying, the question here is not about real weaknesses such as are created by the opponent with threats of attack on the pawn.
zh: 由此可以得出结论：中心兵乃至任何兵之所以容易变弱，一个重要原因就是无法得到相邻线上己方兵的保护。当然，还须结合对手能否对这只兵制造实际攻击威胁来判断。
editorial_note: 用户已确认保留现有中文译文，删除待确认校勘注。

text: This is why the isolation of the central pawns, if they turn out to be on open files, can prove to be a dangerous weakness in a position.
zh: 因此，中心兵一旦孤立，又处于开放线上，就可能成为局面中的危险弱点。

text: The theme “isolated pawn" was treated in the positional teachings of Steinitz and was frequently encountered in tournament practice of the last decade of the 19th century - the period of the formation of these teachings and their baptism in battle.
zh: “孤兵”是斯坦尼茨局面理论中的一个主题。在十九世纪最后十年的比赛实践中，这个主题经常出现；那也正是这套理论逐渐形成并接受实战检验的时期。

text: The struggle around the isolated pawn developed in an interesting way in the game Showalter–Blackburne (Nürnberg 1896):
zh: 肖瓦尔特对布莱克本一局（纽伦堡，1896年），围绕孤兵展开了一场有趣的斗争。

text: The isolated pawn on d4 is a source of serious worry for White.
zh: d4孤兵令白方深感忧虑。

text: Black has prospects of further increasing the attack by... Nf5. The need to defend the pawn limits the activity of the White pieces. Therefore he rightly sees his chances in an attack on the opponent's king's flank, weakened by the removal of all pieces from it and the move... h6. However, 31. Rg3, which suggests itself, does not work as it is possible to simply take the pawn: 31... Rxd4, and if 32 Qxh6, then 32... Ng6. In view of this Showalter stopped at another continuation. **31. Qf4!**
zh:
黑方还准备以...Nf5进一步加强攻击。保兵的任务限制了白方子力的活动。因此，白方把希望寄托在进攻对手王翼上是正确的：黑方全部棋子都已离开王翼，...h6又削弱了这一翼。不过，看似自然的31. Rg3并不奏效，黑方可以直接31... Rxd4吃兵；若32. Qxh6，则32... Ng6。因此，肖瓦尔特选择了另一种后续手段。

**31. Qf4!**

text: White intends to play 32. Rf3, and if 32... f6, then now 33. Rg3. Besides this, the reply 31... Nf5 is parried, on which would follow 32. d5!. Showalter's move is well thought out but it turns out that he did not calculate the future variations to the end. **31... e5**
zh:
白方准备32. Rf3；若32... f6，这时才走33. Rg3。这步动后也应对了31... Nf5，因为白方可32. d5!。肖瓦尔特的构思颇为周到，可惜他没有把后续变化算到底。

**31... e5**

text: This amusing but not dangerous attempt to cut the “Gordian Knot" apparently took Showalter unawares.
zh: 黑方试图以这种有趣、但并不真正危险的方式快刀斩乱麻，看来令肖瓦尔特措手不及。

text: But this is already an unfortunate mistake. White keeps the pawn, but loses a piece, whereas 32. Qe4 would allow him to achieve a draw. For example, 32... exd4 (is there any better?) 33. Qxe7 Re6 34. Qc7 Re1+ 35. Kh2 Qxc7+ 36. Rxc7 Rxb1 37. Rxb7 a5 38. Rf3! f6 39. Rg3 g5 40. hxg5 hxg5 41. Rh3 d3 42. Rhh7 - draw. **32... Re6 33. Qc7 Re1+ 34. Kh2 Qxc7+ 35. Rxc7 Nd5** and Black won. In conclusion we look at several games in full, which help us to understand more deeply the methods of planning, when a weakness in the centre serves as a special purpose object of the plan.
zh:
这就成了令人遗憾的错误：白方保住了兵，却要失子。32. Qe4则可以求和。例如32... exd4（还有更好的选择吗？）33. Qxe7 Re6 34. Qc7 Re1+ 35. Kh2 Qxc7+ 36. Rxc7 Rxb1 37. Rxb7 a5 38. Rf3! f6 39. Rg3 g5 40. hxg5 hxg5 41. Rh3 d3 42. Rhh7，和棋。

**32... Re6 33. Qc7 Re1+ 34. Kh2 Qxc7+ 35. Rxc7 Nd5**

黑方获胜。

最后再看几盘完整例局，深入理解如何以中心弱点为特定目标来制定计划。

text: Queen's Pawn Opening
zh: 后兵开局

text: White: K.Bardeleben
zh: 白方：K. 巴德莱本

text: Black: M.Chigorin
zh: 黑方：M. 齐果林

text: (Hastings 1895)
zh: （黑斯廷斯，1895年）

text: The opening proceeds calmly. Both opponents are busy with the mobilisation of forces, concentrating their influence on the centre. Such “"quiet" conditions are always created when there is a lack of pawn tension in the centre. In the Queen's Pawn Opening this tension is usually conditioned by the moves c4 and... c5. **5... Ngf6 6. Bb2 Bd6 7. Nbd2 c6 8. Ne5**
zh:
开局进程平静。双方都在调动子力，集中力量影响中心。中心没有兵的紧张时，往往就会出现这种“平静”局面。在后兵开局中，通常要通过c4和...c5才能形成这种紧张。

**5... Ngf6 6. Bb2 Bd6 7. Nbd2 c6 8. Ne5**

text: Occupying the e5 square is more effective when the queen's bishop is placed on c8. In the present position it is hard to link this raid to any sort of concrete plan. Besides this, the position of the knight on e5 is only superficially firm. As Black has counterplay with the move... c5, the move Ne5 turns out to be a blank shot.
zh: 黑方后翼象仍在c8时，以马占据e5会更有效。当前局面下，很难把这次跃马与任何具体计划联系起来。此外，e5马的位置也只是表面稳固。黑方能够以...c5反击，这步Ne5实际上成了空放一枪。

text: It would be useful to complete his development (8. O-O) and strive for tension-play in the centre by c4. In this case, White could count on approximate equality. In view of his unassuming play in the opening, he cannot reckon on more.
zh: 白方应先8. O-O完成出子，再以c4争取在中心制造紧张。这样，他可以期待大致均势。开局下得如此平淡，本来也不能奢望更多。

text: White must already defend himself - the win of a pawn is threatened after... cxd4.
zh: 白方已经必须防守：黑方威胁...cxd4后得兵。

text: Indirectly defending the a2 pawn, but the right reply was 14. a4, and if 14... Bb4, then 15. Nb1. White's plan should be to neutralise the pressure on the c-file by c3, and then attempt to carry out active operations on the king's flank.
zh: 间接保护a2兵，但正确的应手是14. a4；若14... Bb4，则15. Nb1。白方的计划应是先以c3化解c线上的压力，再尝试在王翼展开积极行动。

text: By exchanging bishops, Black weakens the c3 square and the d4 pawn. Now he seizes the initiative.
zh: 黑方通过兑象削弱c3格和d4兵，就此夺得主动权。

text: **15. Bxa3 Qxa3**
zh: **15. Bxa3 Qxa3**

text: Black cannot take the pawn on a2 but, by combining pressure on the c-file with an attack on the d4 pawn by the manoeuvre... Qd6-b6, he threatens to consolidate his positional advantage.
zh: 黑方虽然不能吃a2兵，却可以在向c线施压的同时，以...Qd6-b6调后攻击d4兵，从而巩固局面优势。

text: Forced: after... Qd6 this move will already be impossible and the c-pawn turns out to be a real weakness.
zh: 被迫的。等黑方走过...Qd6，这步冲兵就已不可能，c兵也会成为真正的弱点。

text: On 16... Qd6 follows of course 17. c5. Now Black threatens this move.
zh: 若立即16... Qd6，白方当然17. c5。现在黑方才真正准备...Qd6。

text: The only possibility of defence was the move 17. b4, pointed out by Pillsbury. But after 17... dxc4 18. Nxc4 Qa6 19. Nd6 Rxc1 20. Rxc1 b5 21. Ne4 Nxe4 22. Qxe4 Qxa2 23. Qc6 Nb6 24. Qxb5 Nd5 Black maintains the initiative.
zh: 唯一的防守机会，是皮尔斯伯里指出的17. b4。但17... dxc4 18. Nxc4 Qa6 19. Nd6 Rxc1 20. Rxc1 b5 21. Ne4 Nxe4 22. Qxe4 Qxa2 23. Qc6 Nb6 24. Qxb5 Nd5之后，黑方仍掌握主动。

text: White now ignores the hidden threat, and the weak d4 pawn soon proves to be indefensible.
zh: 白方无视了这个潜在威胁，d4弱兵很快便会无力防守。

text: Now the threat... dxc4, with... Qxd4+ to follow, is irresistible.
zh: 现在，...dxc4再...Qxd4+的威胁已无法阻止。

text: **18. Ne5 dxc4 19. Rxc4 b5! 20. Rxc8 Qxd4+ 21. Kh1 Rxc8**
zh: **18. Ne5 dxc4 19. Rxc4 b5! 20. Rxc8 Qxd4+ 21. Kh1 Rxc8**

text: The first stage of the plan was the creation of weaknesses in White's position, in particular the weak pawn on d4, the second - the victorious attack on this pawn. Now approaches the third stage realisation of the advantage.
zh: 计划的第一阶段，是在白方阵地中制造弱点，尤其是d4弱兵；第二阶段，是成功进攻这只兵；现在则进入第三阶段：兑现优势。

text: **22. Ndf3 Qxf4 23. Nxd7 Nxd7 24. Qxb5 Nf6 25. Ng5 Qc7 26. Nxf7**
zh: **22. Ndf3 Qxf4 23. Nxd7 Nxd7 24. Qxb5 Nf6 25. Ng5 Qc7 26. Nxf7**

text: A mistaken sacrifice, but in a hopeless position.
zh: 错误的弃子，但局面本来已经无望。

text: **26... Qxf7 27. Qe5** 27. g5 does not win back the piece in view of... Qd7. **27... Qd7 28. Re1 Qd5+ 29. Qxd5 exd5 30. Re7 Rc1+ 0-1**
Queen's Gambit
zh: 后翼弃兵

text: White: F.Dus Chotimirsky
zh: 白方：F. 杜斯-霍季米尔斯基

text: Black:P.Romanovsky
zh: 黑方：P. 罗曼诺夫斯基

text: (4th USSR Championship 1925)
zh: （第四届苏联锦标赛，1925年）

text: **1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nc3 c5 5. cxd5 exd5 6. g3 Nc6 7. Bg2 Be7**
zh: **1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nc3 c5 5. cxd5 exd5 6. g3 Nc6 7. Bg2 Be7**

text: As a result of a little transposition of moves, a position from one of the main variations of the Tarrasch Defence has arisen. White stops at a plan, the author of which was the famous Russian grandmaster Rubinstein and which is based on a persistent attack on the d5 pawn.
zh: 经过稍许次序转换，双方进入塔拉什防御的一个主要变例。白方选择的计划由俄国名将鲁宾斯坦创立，其核心是持续攻击d5兵。

text: It should be mentioned that Rubinstein's plan brought quite a lot of distress to advocates of Tarrasch's idea.
zh: 值得一提的是，鲁宾斯坦的计划曾使塔拉什构想的支持者们吃尽苦头。

text: This exchange, in connection with the two following moves, is the starting point of a plan which White successfully employed in the game Reti-Tarrasch, in the Pistyan International tournament 1922.
zh: 这次兑换结合白方接下来的两步，是整套计划的起点。1922年皮斯蒂安国际大赛的列蒂对塔拉什一局，白方曾成功运用这一计划。

text: Only here, otherwise 11. Bg5.
zh: 只能退到这里，否则11. Bg5。

text: White will occupy the important d4 point, in connection with which the isolated pawn on d5, pinned down, could become the object of a dangerous attack, as has occurred in many games played with the present variation.
zh: 白方将占据重要的d4格。d5孤兵一旦被限制活动，就可能成为强大攻势的目标；这个变例的许多实战已经出现过这种情况。

text: Here also 11... b6 (thus played Tarrasch in the above mentioned game with Reti), 11... Ng4 and 11... Ne4, have been tried, but all these continuations do not solve the difficult problems arising for Black because of the d5 pawn.
zh: 这里还曾有人尝试11... b6——塔拉什在前述对列蒂一局中就是这样走的——以及11... Ng4和11... Ne4。但这些后续手段都未能彻底解决d5兵给黑方带来的难题。

text: With the move in the game Black intends to effect an exchange of the white-squared bishops after Be4, mistakenly supposing that this strengthens the d5 pawn. Admittedly, one of the White pieces attacking the pawn vanishes from the board, but, as you see, at the same time the Black piece defending it also vanishes. However, it is not the weakness of the d5 pawn, but the control of the strategical square d4, which has decisive significance. The struggle for this square is also Black's main task.
zh: 黑方准备以...Be4交换白格象，误以为这样可以巩固d5兵。诚然，攻击这只兵的一只白子会离开棋盘，但保护它的一只黑子也会同时消失。真正具有决定意义的，倒不只是d5兵的弱点，而是对战略要点d4格的控制。争夺这个格，才是黑方的主要任务。

text: The relatively best reply was 11 Ne4.
zh: 相对而言，11... Ne4是最好的应手。

text: The simplest and most consistent. The blockade of the d5 pawn is guaranteed.
zh: 最简单，也最贯彻计划。白方对d5兵的封锁已经有了保障。

text: On 13... Ne5 would have followed 14. f3 Bg6 15. Bf4 Nc4 16. b3 Nd6 17. Bh3 Nh5 18. Be3, and Black's position remains difficult. Likewise also 13... Bxg2 14. Nxc6 bxc6 15. Kxg2 Qd7 16. Bc5 was clearly to White's advantage. **14. Qxd4 Bxg2 15. Kxg2 b6**
zh:
若13... Ne5，则14. f3 Bg6 15. Bf4 Nc4 16. b3 Nd6 17. Bh3 Nh5 18. Be3，黑方仍然困难。13... Bxg2 14. Nxc6 bxc6 15. Kxg2 Qd7 16. Bc5同样明显有利于白方。

**14. Qxd4 Bxg2 15. Kxg2 b6**

text: Necessary, in order to free the rook from defence of the a7 pawn.
zh: 必要的一步，使车不必再守a7兵。

text: **16. Rfd1 Qd7 17. Nc3 Bc5 18. Qf4 Bxe3 19. Qxe3 Rfe8 20. Qf4 Re6 21. Rd4!**
zh: **16. Rfd1 Qd7 17. Nc3 Bc5 18. Qf4 Bxe3 19. Qxe3 Rfe8 20. Qf4 Re6 21. Rd4!**

text: The d5 pawn is doomed. The whole White army is now hurled into an attack on the isolated outpost.
zh: d5兵在劫难逃，白方全部兵力都投入了对这个孤立据点的围攻。

text: On 22... Rd6 follows 23. e4.
White could win the d5 pawn at once by 23. e4, easily deciding the game. If, on this, 23... Rh5, then 24. h4. **23... h6 24. e3 Qc6**
zh:
白方本可立即23. e4吃掉d5兵，轻松决定胜负。若23... Rh5，则24. h4。

**23... h6 24. e3 Qc6**

text: Black is powerless to defend the pawn. For example, 24... Rh5 25. h4 Ree5 26. e4! dxe4 (26... Nxe4 27. Rxe4! dxe4 28. Qxh5!) 27. Nxe4 Qc6 28. Nxf6+ Qxf6 29. Qxf6 gxf6 30. Rg4+ Kf8 (or 30... Kh7 31. Rd8 Rhf5 32. Rgg8 and wins) 31. Rd8+ Ke7 32. Rgg8 f5 33. Rge8+ Kf6 34. Rxe5 Kxe5 35. f4 remaining to all intents and purposes with an extra rook. **25. Nxd5 Ne4**
zh:
黑方无力保住这只兵。例如24... Rh5 25. h4 Ree5 26. e4! dxe4（26... Nxe4 27. Rxe4! dxe4 28. Qxh5!）27. Nxe4 Qc6 28. Nxf6+ Qxf6 29. Qxf6 gxf6 30. Rg4+ Kf8（或30... Kh7 31. Rd8 Rhf5 32. Rgg8，白方获胜）31. Rd8+ Ke7 32. Rgg8 f5 33. Rge8+ Kf6 34. Rxe5 Kxe5 35. f4，白方实际上等于多出一车。

**25. Nxd5 Ne4**

text: In the search for chance possibilities. Of course, by playing 25... Nxd5 26. Rxd5 Rxd5 27. Rxd5, it was possible to drag on resistance, but with highly problematical hopes of success. **26. Nc3 f5**
zh:
黑方寄希望于偶然的战术机会。当然，25... Nxd5 26. Rxd5 Rxd5 27. Rxd5可以延长抵抗，但挽救败局的希望十分渺茫。

**26. Nc3 f5**

text: The continuation 26... Rf5 27. Qxf5 Nxc3+ 28. Qf3 Qxf3+ 29. Kxf3 Nxd1 30. Rxd1 Rc8 31. Rd2 likewise should not save Black, even though it did not provide White with such a quick celebration of victory.
zh: 26... Rf5 27. Qxf5 Nxc3+ 28. Qf3 Qxf3+ 29. Kxf3 Nxd1 30. Rxd1 Rc8 31. Rd2同样应当救不了黑方，只是白方不会像实战这样快获胜。

text: With several threats; White at least wins one more pawn.
zh: 同时制造多种威胁，白方至少还能再得一兵。

text: **30... Kf7** Or 30... Kh8 31. Ne7 Qb5 32. Qxf5 Qxf5 33. Rxe8+ with an extra rook. **31. Qxf5+ Nf6 32. Rxe8 Kxe8 33. Qe5+ Kf8 34. e4 Nd7 35. Qe7+ Kg8 36. h4 Nc5 37. Qxa7 1-0**
zh:
**30... Kf7**

若30... Kh8，则31. Ne7 Qb5 32. Qxf5 Qxf5 33. Rxe8+，白方多一车。

**31. Qxf5+ Nf6 32. Rxe8 Kxe8 33. Qe5+ Kf8 34. e4 Nd7 35. Qe7+ Kg8 36. h4 Nc5 37. Qxa7 1-0**

text: A valuable game, reflecting clearly three stages of a single plan. The first stage (9th-12th moves) organising objects of attack (the d4 and d5 points). The second stage (from the 13th to 25th moves) carrying out concrete ideas with the aim of winning the d5 pawn. The third stage - realisation of material and positional advantages. Black's manoeuvre... Bf5-e4 turned out to be mistaken.
zh: 这是一盘很有价值的对局，清楚展示了同一计划的三个阶段。第一阶段，第9至第12步，确立攻击目标d4和d5两格；第二阶段，第13至第25步，实施具体构想，吃掉d5兵；第三阶段，兑现子力与局面优势。黑方的...Bf5-e4调象方案被证明是错误的。

text: Four Knights Game
zh: 四马开局

text: White: O.Duras
zh: 白方：O. 杜拉斯

text: Black: A.Rubinstein
zh: 黑方：A. 鲁宾斯坦

text: (Carlsbad 1907)
zh: （卡尔斯巴德，1907年）

text: Before going over to a discussion of this game, we want to say a few words about its epos, if we may express it so, and the author itself of this epos, a classic strategical plan of Rubinstein.
zh: 在讨论本局之前，我们先简述它的主线——如果可以这样称呼——以及这一经典战略计划的创作者鲁宾斯坦。

text: There is a quiet opening, where the first skirmish in the centre is a long time coming, and does not bring an advantage to either side. White begins the offensive first with the move f4, which had been tried time and again in practice and, up to this game, given good results for White. Even in the opening stage, Rubinstein thought out a plan of attack on the e4 square and foresaw that it would be weakened by the move f4. The attack launched by White looked dangerous, but required energetic and purposeful execution. Duras was not able to permeate his play with concrete ideas, to map out a clear outline of the objective and a real way of achieving it. Separate passive moves began to interrupt the planned line of his thoughts, the attack came to assume a shapeless character, whereas Rubinstein continued purposefully force pressure on the e4 pawn. Soon this pressure was converted to an energetic attack by nearly all the Black pieces. The central stronghold of White's position - the e4 pawn fell, and this led to a disintegration of his king's flank.
zh: 开局平静，中心的第一次交锋迟迟才发生，而且没有使任何一方获利。白方率先以f4展开攻势；这种下法此前已在实战中反复出现，并一直给白方带来好结果。鲁宾斯坦却早在开局阶段便想好了进攻e4格的计划，预见到f4将使它削弱。白方的进攻看似危险，却必须有力而有目的地实施。杜拉斯未能使行棋贯穿具体构想，既没有确定清晰的目标，也没有找到切实可行的实现路径。一些消极招法不断打断原有思路，攻势逐渐失去章法；鲁宾斯坦则始终有目的地加强对e4兵的压力。这种压力很快变成几乎全部黑子共同参与的猛烈围攻。白方阵地的中心支柱——e4兵——终于倒下，王翼也随之瓦解。

text: This game, played by Rubinstein at the outset of his creative growth, is a forerunner of all his future versatile work in the area of the opening, ending and principally in the planning struggle of the central stage.
zh: 这盘棋下于鲁宾斯坦创作生涯的早期，已预示了他后来在开局、残局，尤其是中局计划性作战方面的多样成就。

text: Rubinstein's mastery charms by its clear form, strictness, rationality. For him, everything was well-measured, stone by stone. He was a master builder of the chess struggle, and precisely for this reason his plans give an impression of solidity and serve as handy material for study. Rubinstein did not like to yield to the area of intuition. He did not confide in many people even his own experiences and again and again was ready to look diligently at each pebble of his building as if he were running across it for the first time.
zh: 鲁宾斯坦的技艺，以结构清晰、严谨而合乎逻辑令人着迷。他的每一步都经过仔细衡量，仿佛一砖一石地建造整场战斗。正因如此，他的计划给人坚实可靠的印象，也成为极佳的学习材料。他不愿轻易把判断交给直觉；甚至对自己的经验也不盲从，而是愿意一再审视自己所建结构中的每一块石头，像初次见到它那样认真。

text: The diligence with which Rubinstein conducted his games, made each plan and successfully carried it out, demonstrated the excellent creative production of a clear intellect and convincing logic. Rubinstein was not a psychologist, not a philosopher, not a daring artist, but a profound connoisseur of true strokes, accurate lines and the clear harmony of thoughts. All these traits of his creativity show through in the present game.
zh: 鲁宾斯坦以极其认真的态度组织对局、制定计划并成功实施，体现出清晰的智慧和令人信服的逻辑。他不是心理学家，不是哲学家，也不是大胆奔放的艺术家，而是深谙准确笔触、严谨线条和思想协调之美的大师。这些创作特点，在本局中都得到了体现。

text: **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bb5 Bb4 5. O-O O-O 6. d3 Bxc3**
zh: **1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bb5 Bb4 5. O-O O-O 6. d3 Bxc3**

text: Black exchanges the knight with the aim of preventing the move Ne2, which is useful for an attack on the king's flank.
zh: 黑方交换这只马，是为了防止白方以后用Ne2组织王翼进攻。

text: An annoying pin, forcing Black to take measures to free himself from it and then already to set about drawing up a plan of play. Meanwhile White prepares his forces for an attack on the king's flank, intending, after appropriate development, to initiate an offensive with the move f4.
zh: 令人不快的牵制。黑方必须先解除牵制，才能从容制定行棋计划。白方则准备好子力，打算在适当出子后以f4发动王翼进攻。

text: Nowadays this is a theoretical position, repeatedly met in practice and subjected to thorough analysis. In the majority opinion, Black's good development and firm position in the centre allows one to talk of equilibrium. However, when the present game was played, the opening idea employed by Duras was relatively new and inspired fear in Black: in 9 cases out of 10 White's attack brought him success. Rubinstein was the first to bring to light reliable methods of defence in this position and likewise a deeply founded motive for a counter-initiative and counter-attack.
zh: 如今，这已是实战中反复出现、经过深入分析的理论局面。一般认为，黑方出子良好，中心稳固，足以维持均势。但在本局进行的年代，杜拉斯采用的开局构想还相当新颖，令黑方颇为忌惮：十局之中约有九局，白方的进攻都能奏效。鲁宾斯坦率先揭示了这一局面中可靠的防守方法，以及有深刻依据的反夺主动与反击构想。

text: Four years later, in a game with Spielmann played in the second Carlsbad tournament, Rubinstein continued 12... Rd8. Then came 13. g3 Qc7 14. Nh4 d5! 15. f4, and Black could win a pawn by 15... Nxe4, without any compensation for the opponent.
zh: 四年后，在第二届卡尔斯巴德大赛对斯皮尔曼时，鲁宾斯坦改走12... Rd8。随后13. g3 Qc7 14. Nh4 d5! 15. f4，黑方本可15... Nxe4得兵，而对手没有任何补偿。

text: In the present game, Rubinstein sticks to another, less energetic but more concealed, plan of attack on the e4 pawn and with this in view he places the king's rook on e8.
zh: 本局中，鲁宾斯坦采用了另一套攻击e4兵的计划，力度稍缓，却更加隐蔽。为此，他把王翼车放到e8。

text: A serious loss of time. It seems White feared the counter-attack ... d5 and in the event of 15. exd5 Nxd5 defended the pawn on c3. The fact of the matter, however, is that, after 14. g3 d5 15. exd5 Nxd5 16. Rxe5 Nxc3 17. Qe1 Na4 18. Bf4, White far outstrips the opponent in development. **14... Bd7 15. g3 Rad8 16. Bg2 Bc8**
zh:
严重浪费时间。白方看来担心...d5反击，希望在15. exd5 Nxd5之后保护c3兵。然而实际上，14. g3 d5 15. exd5 Nxd5 16. Rxe5 Nxc3 17. Qe1 Na4 18. Bf4之后，白方在出子上遥遥领先。

**14... Bd7 15. g3 Rad8 16. Bg2 Bc8**

text: This bishop later transfers to b7, where it joins in the attack on the e4 pawn. Thus, move by move, sensibly and persistently, Black deploys his forces for a counterattack in the centre.
zh: 这只象以后将转到b7，加入对e4兵的攻击。黑方就这样一步一步，合理而坚定地部署子力，准备在中心反击。

text: White has a mobile pawn centre, further reinforced by the f4 pawn. True, his queen's side forces are still not mobilised, his king's position is rather exposed. Nevertheless, the strong central pawn group opens up good prospects for White for the future. He should only base his concrete ideas on a plan, remembering that an extremely sharp situation demands a dynamic approach to the position. You see, all of Black's pieces will be on central squares, therefore it is necessary to carry out the attack quickly and energetically.
zh: 白方拥有能够向前冲击的兵中心，并得到f4兵的进一步支持。诚然，他的后翼子力尚未充分调动，王的位置也比较暴露；但强大的中心兵群仍给他带来良好前景。白方必须围绕计划形成具体构想，牢记尖锐的局面要求以动态方式处理。黑方全部子力都将集中到中心，因此白方的进攻必须迅速而有力。

text: A crafty retreat. Black intends to play... Ng6 and, by removing White's knight, increase still further the pressure on the centre.
zh: 巧妙的退马。黑方准备...Ng6，赶走白马，进一步加强对中心的压力。

text: He would like to play 19. e5, but after 19... Ng6 20. Nxg6 hxg6 21. Ba3 Bf5 22. Bxd6 Qxd6 23. exd6 Bxd3 24. cxd3 Rxd6 and Black has the better endgame.
zh: 白方很想走19. e5，但19... Ng6 20. Nxg6 hxg6 21. Ba3 Bf5 22. Bxd6 Qxd6 23. exd6 Bxd3 24. cxd3 Rxd6之后，黑方的残局更好。

text: With the move in the game, White prevents the entry of the knight on g6 and threatens to play Bg5. The reply is forced.
zh: 实战这步冲兵阻止黑马进入g6，并威胁Bg5，黑方的应手是被迫的。

text: Beginning play without a plan and this in a tense position, where each move must be with an objective. White should combine the threat of a break in the centre (e5) with an attack on the g-file (Kh1, Rg1 etc). In the first instance, 20. Bf4 with the threat e5 serves for the carrying out of this plan. After the probable 20... Nh5 21. Bg3 Nh7 there is a tense struggle in prospect with chances for both sides.
zh: 白方开始无计划地行棋，而在这样紧张的局面中，每一步都必须有明确目标。白方应把中心e5冲兵突破的威胁，与g线上的进攻结合起来，例如Kh1、Rg1等。首先应20. Bf4，威胁e5，以贯彻这一计划。较可能的20... Nh5 21. Bg3 Nh7之后，双方都将有机会，战斗仍然紧张。

text: White again begins to solve a particular problem - to prevent the knight going to g5. A little more and his whole game will go downhill.
zh: 白方又只顾解决局部问题：不让黑马到g5。再这样下去，整个局面就会迅速恶化。

text: He should play 21. Qg3 Qe7 22. Bf3 (but not 22. Bxh6? Nh5 23. Qg4 N7f6 24. Qg5 Kh7, and White suffers material loss) and the decisive battle is still ahead. **21... Re7 22. h4?** Even now, after 22. e5 dxe5 23. Rxe5 Rxe5 24. Nxe5, despite the pawn weaknesses, White would have a satisfactory position thanks to the active deployment of his pieces.
zh:
白方应走21. Qg3 Qe7 22. Bf3，而不能22. Bxh6? Nh5 23. Qg4 N7f6 24. Qg5 Kh7，遭受子力损失。这样，决定性的战斗仍在后面。

**21... Re7 22. h4?**

即使到此时，22. e5 dxe5 23. Rxe5 Rxe5 24. Nxe5也能给白方带来尚可的局面；尽管兵形有弱点，他的子力却十分活跃。

text: Little by little beginning preparations for a counter-attack, which leads to a decisive result sooner than could be imagined.
zh: 黑方开始逐步准备反击，而反击取得决定性成果的速度，远比预想的快。

text: ... c4 is threatened, winning a pawn. If 23. dxc5, then 23... dxc5 24. Qc4 Ng4 with increasing threats. **23. Nh2 Rde8 24. Re3**
zh:
黑方威胁...c4得兵。若23. dxc5，则23... dxc5 24. Qc4 Ng4，威胁不断增加。

**23. Nh2 Rde8 24. Re3**

text: The only reply, but it merely postpones the downfall of the central pawns.
zh: 唯一的应手，但只是推迟中心兵的覆灭。

text: The loss of a pawn could be delayed by the move 26. d5, but the surrender of the e5 square would be an even greater loss, while the pawn all the same would prove to be doomed to destruction. On 26. d5 might follow 26... Nd7 27. Bg2 Ne5 28. Qf1 Nf6 29. Kh1 Qc8 and then ... Ba6 with the gain of territory. **26... c4**
zh:
26. d5可以暂缓丢兵，但让出e5格会造成更大损失，兵最终仍保不住。例如26... Nd7 27. Bg2 Ne5 28. Qf1 Nf6 29. Kh1 Qc8，再...Ba6，黑方进一步夺取空间。

**26... c4**

text: The inevitable has happened! The main point of the defence has fallen, after a few moves all is lost.
zh: 不可避免的事情终于发生了！白方防线的主要支点倒下，再过几步便全盘皆输。

text: **28. Qg2 d5 29. Bc1 Bxf3 30. Nxf3 Rxe3 31. Bxe3 Re4 32. Qh3 Rg4+ 33. Kh1 Rg3 34. Qh2 Ng4 35. Bg1** Or 35. Qe2 Rxf3. **35... Nxh2 36. Bxh2 Qf4 37. Ng1 Qxh4 0-1**
zh:
**28. Qg2 d5 29. Bc1 Bxf3 30. Nxf3 Rxe3 31. Bxe3 Re4 32. Qh3 Rg4+ 33. Kh1 Rg3 34. Qh2 Ng4 35. Bg1**

或35. Qe2 Rxf3。

**35... Nxh2 36. Bxh2 Qf4 37. Ng1 Qxh4 0-1**

text: Nimzo-Indian Defence
zh: 列蒂开局
editorial_note: 用户确认本局开局应为列蒂开局，中文标题据此改正并删除待确认校勘注；英文原书标题保留备查。本次订正仅针对本局。

text: White:M.Botvinnik
zh: 白方：M. 鲍特维尼克

text: Black: E.Zagorovsky
zh: 黑方：E. 扎戈罗夫斯基

text: (Sverdlovsk 1943)
zh: （斯维尔德洛夫斯克，1943年）

text: After this display of activity White gets the chance to begin play on the isolated d5 pawn, and on the basis of this achievement, sets about the construction of a great plan. Nevertheless it is hard to blame him for striving for lively play and opening the position in the centre, the more so that other less active continuations have their shady sides. Both 6... b6 7. Ne5 Bb7 8. Be2 Nbd7 9. f4 and 6... Nbd7 7. Be2 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Nd4 would secure White the better prospects. **7. cxd5 Nxd5 8. Nxd5 exd5**
zh:
黑方这一积极行动，使白方有机会围绕d5孤兵展开战斗，并据此制定一套完整计划。不过，很难责怪黑方力求活跃、打开中心的意图，何况其他较缓和的后续手段也有缺点。无论6... b6 7. Ne5 Bb7 8. Be2 Nbd7 9. f4，还是6... Nbd7 7. Be2 b6 8. cxd5 exd5 9. Nd4，都将给白方更好的前景。

**7. cxd5 Nxd5 8. Nxd5 exd5**

text: The capture 8... Qxd5 would allow White to develop his bishop with tempo, since on 9. Bc4 he would have to retreat the queen to d8; 9... Qh5 is worse in view of 10. g4!.
zh: 8... Qxd5会使白方出象并抢得先手，因为9. Bc4之后黑后必须退回d8；9... Qh5因10. g4!而更差。

text: White's plan is clear. The first stage of it is the creation of an isolated pawn on d5.
zh: 白方的计划很清楚，第一阶段是在d5制造孤兵。

text: **9... cxd4** If 9... Qa5+, then 10. Qd2 Qxd2+ 11. Kxd2. On 9... Bf6 good is 10. Qd2 b6 11. Be2. Sooner or later, after dxc5, Black gets "hanging" pawns, which in the present situation turns out to be a weakness in his position. Therefore Black himself exchanges on d4, conceding the “isolated" pawn on d5; at least it is unfavourable for White to take on d4 now either with the knight, in view of... Bb4+, or with the bishop because of... Nc6. **10. Qxd4 Bf6 11. Qd2 Nc6 12. Be2** **12... Be6**
zh:
**9... cxd4**

若9... Qa5+，则10. Qd2 Qxd2+ 11. Kxd2。对9... Bf6，10. Qd2 b6 11. Be2很好。白方迟早会dxc5，使黑方形成悬兵；在当前条件下，这将成为黑方的弱点。因此，黑方主动在d4交换，接受d5孤兵。至少现在白方不宜用马吃回，因为...Bb4+；也不宜用象吃回，因为...Nc6。

**10. Qxd4 Bf6 11. Qd2 Nc6 12. Be2**

**12... Be6**

text: The beginning of an incorrect plan. Black limits his activity to defence of the d5 pawn, whereas it was necessary for him at all costs to prevent White's capturing the d4 square. It is even worth giving up a pawn for this by... d4. There was, however, a better possibility: 12... Bxb2 13. Qxb2 Qa5+ 14. Qd2 Qxd2+ 15. Kxd2 d4 16. exd4 Rd8 17. Kc3 Bg4 18. Rhd1 Rac8 and Black ought not lose. **13. O-O Bxb2 14. Qxb2 Qa5 15. Rfd1 Rfd8 16. Rd2 Rd7 17. Rad1 Rad8 18. h3 h6 19. Ne5 Nxe5 20. Qxe5 Qc5 21. Bf3**
zh:
错误计划的开端。黑方把全部行动局限于保卫d5兵，但他本应不惜代价阻止白方控制d4格；为此，甚至以...d4弃兵也值得考虑。不过，此时还有更好的办法：12... Bxb2 13. Qxb2 Qa5+ 14. Qd2 Qxd2+ 15. Kxd2 d4 16. exd4 Rd8 17. Kc3 Bg4 18. Rhd1 Rac8，黑方应当不会输。

**13. O-O Bxb2 14. Qxb2 Qa5 15. Rfd1 Rfd8 16. Rd2 Rd7 17. Rad1 Rad8 18. h3 h6 19. Ne5 Nxe5 20. Qxe5 Qc5 21. Bf3**

text: The second part of White's plan consisted of riveting the whole of Black's forces to the weak central pawn. This objective has been achieved and the denouement draws closer.
zh: 白方计划的第二阶段，是把黑方全部子力牵制在中心弱兵的防守上。这个目标已经实现，决战即将到来。

text: He should simply give up the pawn by playing 23... Qc7 or 23 Qc3.
zh: 黑方应干脆放弃这只兵，走23... Qc7或23... Qc3。

text: The concluding phase of the plan. Exploiting the fact that Black's pieces have been diverted to defence of the centre, White launches an attack on the king's flank.
zh: 计划进入最后阶段。白方利用黑方子力都被牵制在中心防守的机会，发动王翼进攻。

text: Kh1 followed by Rg1 is threatened, after which the attack on the h and g-files proves to be irresistible.
zh: 威胁Kh1再Rg1，此后沿h线和g线的进攻将势不可挡。

text: With the aim of establishing a link for the queen to the king's flank, but now new weak squares on e5 and g5 are created.
zh: 黑方试图为后打通通往王翼的线路，却又在e5、g5制造了新的弱格。

text: Black's position is miserable, but this move, locking in the king, facilitates White's final attack.
zh: 黑方的局面本已糟糕，这步棋又堵住王的退路，使白方最后的进攻更加容易。

text: The weak d5 pawn, the culprit for all Black's trouble in this game, remained intact, but the king perished.
zh: d5弱兵是本局黑方所有麻烦的根源；它最终仍然安然无恙，王却丧命了。

text: Queen's Gambit
zh: 后翼弃兵

text: White: H.Kmoch
zh: 白方：H. 克莫赫

text: Black: A.Alekhine
zh: 黑方：A. 阿廖欣

text: (Kecskemet 1927)
zh: （凯奇凯梅特，1927年）

text: White conducts the opening rather planlessly, but, by playing 7. Nc3 now, he could count on equality. Instead of this, White, at the cost of the loss of a tempo, provokes Black into a... favourable exchange for himself - favourable because even from the first opening moves he was thinking of an operation to seize the white squares.
zh: 白方开局下得颇无计划，但此时7. Nc3仍可期待均势。他却宁愿损失一个先手，诱使黑方作出一次……对黑方有利的兑换！它之所以有利，是因为黑方从开局最初几步起，就在考虑如何控制白格。

text: An interesting and original plan, particularly if it is taken into account that the knight cannot be maintained on e4. Black wants to exchange both knights and provoke the opponent into the advance e4, weakening the central pawns. White does not discover the opponent's plan and willingly goes halfway to meeting this idea...
zh: 这是一个有趣而独特的计划，尤其考虑到黑马无法长期留在e4，就更显其巧思。黑方准备兑换双方各一只马，并诱使白方冲起e4，削弱中心兵。白方没有察觉对手的计划，反而乐于配合。

text: **9. Nfd2 Ndf6 10. Nc3 Nxd2 11. Bxd2 Be7 12. e4**
zh: **9. Nfd2 Ndf6 10. Nc3 Nxd2 11. Bxd2 Be7 12. e4**

text: Black also reckoned on this. Now he obtains an object for pressure - the d4 pawn.
zh: 这正是黑方期待的。他现在获得了施压目标：d4兵。

text: Not a bad position for the bishop, but if White's game were permeated with a concrete plan, he would without difficulty have found a better scheme of deploying his pieces.
zh: 象放在这里不坏，但如果白方的行棋始终贯穿具体计划，他就不难找到更好的子力部署。

text: Taking into account the potential weakness of the d4 pawn, White ought to imagine the way Black will go about organising pressure on this point. He will obviously play the queen to c7, and then place one of the rooks on the open file. In order to prevent this, it was necessary to place the bishop not on c3, but on f4, and then play Rad1 and Be5. A tense struggle arises with chances for both sides.
zh: 考虑到d4兵可能变弱，白方应预见黑方将如何组织压力：显然，黑后会到c7，再把一只车放到开放线上。为了阻止这一部署，白象不应放在c3，而应放到f4，再走Rad1和Be5。这样将形成双方都有机会的紧张战斗。

text: In place of this, after a few moves White falls into the worse position. Neglect of a concrete idea, this most important element of planning, frequently leads to such results.
zh: 实战中，白方却在几步之后便落入劣势。忽视具体构想这一计划中最重要的要素，常常会导致这样的结果。

text: Black carries out his contemplated set-up. Now the variation 16. d5 cxd5 17. Nxf6+ gxf6 is favourable for him, but not 17... Bxf6 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Qf3 Qxc4 20. Qxf6 Qe4 21. Rfe1 Qg6 22. Qd4 Qg7 23. Re5, and White's attack compensates for the pawn. **16. Rd2?**
zh:
黑方完成了预定部署。现在16. d5 cxd5 17. Nxf6+ gxf6有利于黑方；但不能17... Bxf6 18. Bxf6 gxf6 19. Qf3 Qxc4 20. Qxf6 Qe4 21. Rfe1 Qg6 22. Qd4 Qg7 23. Re5，白方的攻势足以补偿少掉的一兵。

**16. Rd2?**

text: White ignores the opponent's threats. He should not allow the invasion of the queen. A quite sufficient defence, securing the position of the d4 pawn, was indicated by Alekhine: 16. f4. Now it is hard for Black to prevent the move f5, eliminating the blockading e6 pawn, while after this the advance d5 becomes only a question of time. For example, 16. f4 Rfe8 17. f5 and 17... e5 is not possible in view of 18. Nxf6+ Bxf6 19. Qg3 (19... Qb6 20. c5 followed by dxe5). **16... Qf4 17. Nxf6+**
zh:
白方无视了对手的威胁，不应容许黑后侵入。阿廖欣指出，16. f4足以防守，并能巩固d4兵。这样黑方便难以阻止f5，白方可消除阻碍d兵前进的e6兵，随后冲起d5只是时间问题。例如16. f4 Rfe8 17. f5，17... e5不行，因为18. Nxf6+ Bxf6 19. Qg3；若19... Qb6，则20. c5，再dxe5。

**16... Qf4 17. Nxf6+**

text: On 17. Re1, there would have probably followed simply 17... Rd7.
zh: 若17. Re1，黑方大概只需17... Rd7。

text: The advance d5 is prevented, and the d4 pawn has become a continual worry for White.
zh: 白方冲起d5的可能性被制止，d4兵成为一个持续的负担。

text: Another weak move, creating new objects of attack for Black. Thus, in due course, arises the threat... g5, indeed also the f4 pawn itself will require defence. Finally, he should pay attention to the weakening of the e4 square, which is increased even more by the position of the queen on f5.
zh: 又是一步软着，为黑方制造了新的攻击目标。黑方以后会有...g5的威胁，f4兵本身也需要保护。此外，还应注意e4格已被削弱，而黑后位于f5又进一步放大了这一弱点。

text: 21... c5 was threatened.
zh: 黑方原先威胁21... c5。

text: A typical blockading move. Black is now master of the white squares.
zh: 典型的封锁手段。黑方已经牢牢掌握白格。

text: The final positional mistake in a bad position. The pawn was obliged to remain on b2, so as to support the c4 pawn by b3 in case of need. Only in this way could White maintain control over the key central d5 square.
zh: 在劣势局面中，又犯下最后一个局面错误。b兵本应留在b2，以便必要时b3保护c4兵。只有这样，白方才能维持对关键中心格d5的控制。

text: In the present example we get to know another important positional function of the pawns: to gain squares for use as handy piece bases.
zh: 通过这个例子，我们认识到兵的另一项重要局面作用：争夺适合己方棋子利用的据点。

text: A standard pawn attack to capture the d5 square.
zh: 典型的兵的攻击，目的是夺取d5格。

text: If he is to die - then let it be with honour! In the event of 23. c5 White would be suffocated and could not defend his weak points on d4 and f4. It is enough for Black to place his rook on d5, play... g6, and transfer the bishop to h6, after which one of the threats... e5 or... g5 proves to be unstoppable. **23... bxc4 24. Qxc6 Qxf4 25. Qxc4 e5**
zh:
即使要输，也要拼个痛快！如果23. c5，白方就会窒息，无法守住d4和f4两个弱点。黑方只需把车放到d5，走...g6，再把象调到h6，...e5或...g5的威胁总有一个无法阻止。

**23... bxc4 24. Qxc6 Qxf4 25. Qxc4 e5**

text: A fifth attack on a fourfold defence.
zh: 四重防守，迎来了第五次攻击。

text: An attempt to steal away with the bishop to e1. Upon the retreat Ba1 or Bb2 would have followed 27... d3!. In addition it seems to White that the d4 pawn is "pinned".
zh: 试图让象悄悄撤到e1。若Ba1或Bb2，则27... d3!。此外，白方似乎还认为d4兵已被“牵制”。

text: **27... dxc3! 28. Rxd7 Rxd7 29. Rxd7** Or 29. Qe8+ Kh7 30. Qxd7 Qe4! 31. Qh3 c2 32. Rf1 Qd4+ 33. Kh1 Qd1 and Black also wins. **29... Bd4+ 30. Kh1 Qc1+ 0-1**

In this game, Kmoch made several tactical errors, the most serious - on the 16th and 22nd moves. However the most cardinal mistake, already of strategical character, was the neglect of the white squares after the exchange of the white-squared bishops, provoked by Kmoch himself in the opening.
zh: 克莫赫本局犯了数个战术错误，以第16步和第22步最为严重。但更根本的错误属于战略层面：他在开局主动促成白格象的交换，却随后忽视了对白格的控制。

text: Queen's Indian Defence
zh: 后印度防御

text: White: M.Euwe
zh: 白方：M. 尤伟

text: Black: A.Alekhine
zh: 黑方：A. 阿廖欣

text: (23rd game, return match 1937)
zh: （1937年世界冠军回敬赛，第23局）

text: In this very interesting game unfolds a creative argument on the theme of “hanging' pawns.
zh: 这盘极有意思的对局，展开了一场围绕悬兵的创造性争论。

text: There is still a great deal of work in prospect for the brains of chess theoreticians and masters in order to bring, as it were, relative clarity into the contradictions of "hanging pawns. These are both a strength and a weakness, both a mechanism of attack and an object of attack itself, both a formation establishing a gain of space in the centre and a building with shaky foundations.
zh: 要相对清楚地解释悬兵的种种矛盾，理论家和大师们仍须付出大量思考：悬兵既是强点又是弱点，既是攻击手段又是受攻目标，既能在中心争得空间，又像一座根基不稳的建筑。

text: The present game is one of the most interesting contributions to the investigation of the problems, brought about by the thoughts of two world champions.
zh: 两位世界冠军的思考，使本局成为研究这一问题时极为精彩的例证。

text: "Hanging" pawns were formed here even in the opening stage, after:
zh: 悬兵早在开局阶段便已形成：

text: **1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. g3 Bb7 5. Bg2 Be7 6. O-O O-O 7. b3 d5 8. Ne5 c5 9. dxc5 bxc5 10. cxd5 exd5 11. Nc3 Nbd7!**
zh: **1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 4. g3 Bb7 5. Bg2 Be7 6. O-O O-O 7. b3 d5 8. Ne5 c5 9. dxc5 bxc5 10. cxd5 exd5 11. Nc3 Nbd7!**

text: Black foresaw this position when, on the 8th move, he began an energetic pawn attack in the centre. Now he completes the mobilisation of his forces and indirectly defends the d5 pawn.
zh: 黑方在第8步开始以兵积极冲击中心时，就已预见到这一局面。现在他完成子力动员，并间接保护d5兵。

text: An excellent reply, containing the threat to increase pressure on the d5 pawn by Nf4. The continuation 12... Ne4 13. Nxe4 dxe4 14. Bb2! does not suit Black now because his pawn position is shattered while White's pieces operate purposefully and harmoniously. **12... Nb6**
zh:
极佳的应手，准备以Nf4增加对d5兵的压力。现在12... Ne4 13. Nxe4 dxe4 14. Bb2!不适合黑方，因为黑方兵形散乱，而白方子力行动明确、配合协调。

**12... Nb6**

text: Apparently firmly defending the d5 pawn, but a possibility is opened for White for an attack on the adjacent c5 pawn. A more reliable defence of the “hanging' pawns could have been organised by playing 12... Qa5. After 13. Bb2 (13. Bd2 Qa6) 13... Rfd8 14. Nf4 Nb6 15. Qe1 (with the threat Nxd5) 15... Kf8, White cannot increase the attack.
zh: 看似牢牢守住d5兵，却让白方有机会攻击相邻的c5兵。12... Qa5可以更可靠地防守悬兵。13. Bb2（13. Bd2 Qa6）13... Rfd8 14. Nf4 Nb6 15. Qe1，威胁Nxd5，15... Kf8之后，白方无法再加强攻击。

text: Surprisingly, White himself weakens the pressure on the central pawn, which allows the opponent to comfortably regroup his pieces. He should continue 15. Nf4 followed by Qd3; the d5 pawn would give Black a lot of trouble.
zh: 令人意外的是，白方自己减轻了对中心兵的压力，使对手能够从容重组子力。他应走15. Nf4再Qd3，d5兵将给黑方带来许多麻烦。

text: Couldn't Black well solve here the problem of the “hanging pawns? Hardly. On 16... c4 would have followed 17. Bxe7 Qxe7 18. Qxa5 cxd3, and the crisis is solved rather in White's favour, for example, 19. Qxb6 dxe2 20. Re1 Nc5 21. Nd4! **17. Rd1 Nd6 18. Nf4**
zh:
黑方此时能否干脆解决悬兵问题？恐怕不行。16... c4会遭到17. Bxe7 Qxe7 18. Qxa5 cxd3，局势的剧变反而更有利于白方。例如19. Qxb6 dxe2 20. Re1 Nc5 21. Nd4!。

**17. Rd1 Nd6 18. Nf4**

text: It seems White's efforts are beginning to bear fruit. However, it soon becomes clear that Black also reckoned precisely on this natural reply and had prepared a surprising counter-blow, which refutes the opponent's plan literally on the threshold of achieving its objective.
zh: 白方的努力似乎开始见效。但很快就会发现，黑方恰恰预料到了这个自然应手，并准备了一记出人意料的反击，在对手即将实现目标之际，将其计划击破。

text: 18. Bh3 offered better chances, with the probable continuation 18... Nxb5 19. axb5 c4 (if 19... d4, then 20. Rc1 with dangerous pressure on the c5 pawn, while against the play on the long diagonal he has a reliable defensive resource - f3) 20. Bxe7 Qxe7 21. bxc4 dxc4 22. Nf4 Rfd8 23. Qxa5. Having an extra pawn and a good position, White has a right to hope for success. **18... Nxb5 19. axb5 Nf6 20. Nxd5**
zh:
18. Bh3提供了更好的机会。较可能的变化是18... Nxb5 19. axb5 c4（若19... d4，则20. Rc1，对c5兵形成危险压力；面对黑方长斜线上的活动，白方还有f3这一可靠防守资源）20. Bxe7 Qxe7 21. bxc4 dxc4 22. Nf4 Rfd8 23. Qxa5。白方多一兵，局面也好，有理由期待获胜。

**18... Nxb5 19. axb5 Nf6 20. Nxd5**

text: The pawn falls, and White is ready to celebrate the occasion of a successfully completed siege of the "hanging" pawns.
zh: 兵终于被吃掉了，白方正准备庆祝对悬兵围攻的成功。

text: Apparently Euwe reckoned now only on the continuation 21... Qb6 22. exd5 Bd6 23. Qe2 Rb8 (threatening to attack the b5 pawn) 24. Rc1 (so as, on 24... Bc8, to reply 25. Qc4) 24... Ba8 25. Qc4 Rfc8 26. Bh3 Rc7 27. Rfe1 and White holds on to the pawn. **21... c4!**
zh:
尤伟看来只考虑了21... Qb6 22. exd5 Bd6 23. Qe2 Rb8，威胁攻击b5兵，24. Rc1，以便对24... Bc8应以25. Qc4，24... Ba8 25. Qc4 Rfc8 26. Bh3 Rc7 27. Rfe1，白方保住多出的一兵。

**21... c4!**

text: With this surprising move Black wins back the pawn, transferring the game into a sharp four-rook endgame. The further course of the game is not relative to the problems of "hanging" pawns, and it is sufficient for us to point out that after **22. Bxe7 Qxe7 23. exd5 Qxe1 24. Rfxe1 cxb3 25. d6 Bxg2 26. Kxg2 Rb8 27. d7 g6?** (Correct is 27... Rfd8 and... Kf8) **28. Ra1?** (A mistake in reply; 28. Rd4 Rfd8 29. Re3 a4 30. Re8+ Rxe8 31. dxe8=Q+ Rxe8 32. Rxa4 and then Rb4 led to a winning position.) **28... Rxb5 29. Re8 Rd5 30. Rxa5 Rxd7 31. Rxf8+ Kxf8 32. Rb5 Rd3** already Black was left with an extra passed and far advanced pawn. However, Alekhine chose an incorrect plan (advance of the pawns on the king's flank), created weaknesses in this sector of the board and Euwe achieved a draw with defensive technique.
zh:
黑方以这步出人意料的冲兵吃回一兵，将对局引入尖锐的四车残局。此后的进程与悬兵问题已无直接关系，因此这里只简要指出：

**22. Bxe7 Qxe7 23. exd5 Qxe1 24. Rfxe1 cxb3 25. d6 Bxg2 26. Kxg2 Rb8 27. d7 g6?**

正确的是27... Rfd8，再...Kf8。

**28. Ra1?**

白方也以错误回应。28. Rd4 Rfd8 29. Re3 a4 30. Re8+ Rxe8 31. dxe8=Q+ Rxe8 32. Rxa4，再Rb4，可以取得胜势。

**28... Rxb5 29. Re8 Rd5 30. Rxa5 Rxd7 31. Rxf8+ Kxf8 32. Rb5 Rd3**

此时，反而是黑方多出一只位置深入的通路兵。然而阿廖欣选择了错误计划——在王翼冲兵，在这一翼制造了弱点。尤伟则凭借防守技术取得和棋。

text: The game reveals well both the positional weakness of “hanging” pawns and their potential strength, consisting of the threat to advance.
zh: 本局既清楚揭示了悬兵在局面上的弱点，也展示了它们潜在的力量：向前冲击的威胁。
